- **Fix**: Widen a hopped part's writes to the new layer's implied writes (or SITE when the new layer's reach is unknown, as a text step's is) at the moment handedRoute replaces the route.

### A38 — Versions and restore

Versions are immutable builds under builds/<slug>/<version>/, each with its client files, server.js, a state snapshot (pages, parts, config, sidecar, kit) and a manifest. The one mutable pointer, current/<slug>.json, names the live build. Older sites can also have legacy copies under versions/<slug>/<id>/, which nothing writes or prunes any more. GET /api/site/<slug>/versions merges both layouts newest first (mergeVersions(listVersions, listBuilds)). listBuilds returns every staged build that has a manifest, and nothing marks which build is live, which was ever published, or which is only a draft. POST …/versions/restore calls restoreVersion (worker.js:13394). A build-layout version is re-activated through activateBuild: a conditional pointer write, the version's whole sidecar, its script, then its state copied into the editable keys, with the head marker written last. A legacy version is copied back over sites/<slug>/ with the sweep, and the pointer is deleted. Back online (site-live.mjs putBackOnline) restores list[0], the newest staged build, and only falls back to a recompile, which draft-first refuses. Neither restore path reads the draft record, the publication journal or the site's publish turn, so with DRAFT_FIRST on they ignore the draft model entirely. A restore never puts back database schema, rows, scheduled jobs or library files. Nightly backups (site-backup.mjs) dump each site's declared tables and an allow-listed slice of _meta to R2 from the cron; they can be downloaded, and there is no restore from them.

| What it does | Shown | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Versions list (GET /versions, both layouts merged, newest first) | live-proven | The canary's RESTORE mode read the site's own list on fold-lane-bakery in run 35: 5 versions, row 1 01789969693841-xqi8vs (docs/investigations/edit-path-checklist.md:8146-8150). This was before DRAFT_FIRST=on, so no draft builds were in the list. |
| Build-layout restore (activation of an older version, state copied back) | live-proven | Run 50 restored 8btpep (edit-path-checklist.md:14, 6296). Free restores in runs 64, 67 and 75 were checked byte for byte (CLAUDE.md, Batch 1 A3 / run 75). All of these ran before DRAFT_FIRST went on (2026-10-17). |
| Restore with DRAFT_FIRST=on and a draft record standing (what happens to the draft, the editable copy and the Publish panel) | untested | No test runs restoreVersion with a draft record. DF6 (test/turn-fence.test.mjs:1069-1080) only checks the source shape, asserting that restoreVersion activates without asDraft. site-busy.test.mjs:754-757 checks only the order of the marker write. |
| Back online through the version path with DRAFT_FIRST=on | untested | PPM4b (test/parallel-publish-media.test.mjs:441-462) passes `versions: async () => []`, so wayBack never takes the version path. Only the recompile refusal is exercised. |
| Legacy-layout restore (rollbackVersion copy, sweep, pointer dropped) | offline-only | test/site-versions.test.mjs and test/site-live.test.mjs run against a fake store. No live run restored a legacy version. |

#### A38-8 · low · unverified · risk

**Restore is not coordinated with an open publication or the site's publish turn**

- **Where**: `worker.js:13394-13432`, `worker.js:13041-13060`, `worker.js:43264-43320`, `docs/history/2026-10-15-draft-first.md:640-652`
- **What**: restoreVersion does not read publishingNow or the journal, and does not take the publish turn. The publication's guard against 'the live site moved on' is checked only in the switching phase. A restore that lands while a publication is in `switched` lets the runner (or the recovery sweep) keep applying that revision's held schema, rows, inserts and media replace/delete over the restored older code, then mark the revision applied. The restore's unfenced writes to source, parts, kit, config and head can also interleave with a turn holder's writes.
- **What goes wrong**: The owner presses Publish on rev 3, which replaces video A and deletes picture P. The switch lands and the finish steps start. The owner, seeing the new pages, immediately restores the previous version from Versions. The sweep finishes rev 3: P is deleted and A's bytes are replaced while the restored pages still show P and A, so P renders broken and A plays the new video.
- **Evidence**: restoreVersion has no publication or turn reads (worker.js:13394-13449). runPublication's `if (liveV !== j.from) return before("the site changed while publishing")` sits inside `if (j.phase === "switching")`. The FINISH block (worker.js:13041 onward) runs without re-reading the pointer.
- **Fix**: Refuse a restore (409) while a publication journal is open, or have the finish phase stop when the pointer no longer names j.version. Take the publish turn for the restore's writes.

### S1 — Seam: Worker ↔ container job

A container job runs worker.js under Node: builder/container-job.mjs calls runContainerJob, and makeContainerEnv builds its env. That env holds the JOB_ENV_NAMES strings, SITES_BUCKET as a GatewayBucket that talks to /api/job/<id>/r2, and SB_MARKER in place of the service key and mint, so gatewayFetch sends service-key calls to /sb. It also carries the JOB_NEXT, JOB_REPLY, JOB_PROGRESS and JOB_SCOPE ops. On the Worker, gatewayHandler admits R2 keys through allowedJobKey, readableJobKey, ownBuildMarker and allowedJobPrefix, and Supabase calls through SB_RPCS and SB_TABLES. Each is bound to the token's id, slug or uid; a pre-scoped first build reaches only jobs/. I went through every key family on the edit, add-on, route-op and build paths. With db4e73e1, the R2 wall covers everything DRAFT_FIRST, PARALLEL_WRITES and REQUEST_FLOW write from a job: site-drafts, preview-*, scriptpending, publish-turn, a read-only request record, jobs/prepared, source/purchases and the builds-live markers. Request records, markers, files and replies are written only by the Worker, which a job reaches through /next. JOB_ENV_NAMES carries every switch the job path reads. REQUEST_FLOW, JOB_RUNNER_*, JOB_MAX_MINUTES and DEPLOY_ID are read only by the Worker, and the SITE_WORKERS, SITE_ROUTES, SITE_API_CACHE and EMAIL bindings are absent by design. The gaps that remain are reads the gateway refuses (a filter that is not the token's slug, or a table or key it does not admit) whose callers quietly treat the 403 as "free" or "unknown": the rename lane's site check, the first build's chat and free-name lookups, pre-site media (drafts/, media-ledger/), neon_teardown, and another job's held checkpoint. takeTurn still turns any storage refusal into a wait that only killing the process ends, and the request driver re-runs a "turn" failure twice.

| A container publish writes builds/, current/, sitemeta/ and sites/ through the R2 gateway | live-proven | Runs 66 and 72 (published li1j0y and yuy16h, 2026-09-29/30). The script-note path (scriptpending/) added later is offline only: rollout checklist §1, the fired-job cases |
| A first build runs pre-scoped in the container and is re-scoped through /scope when the designer names the site | live-proven | First builds have run in the container since 2026-09-14 (JOB_RUNNER_EVERYONE); run 117 recorded in docs/backlog.md ('First builds no longer took the parallel design') |

For a live site, the held rename is accepted into the draft ('When you publish, your site moves to…') and then refused at Publish. On deploy 2215 this is hidden only because every edit stops earlier at its source read (S1-2); deploying db4e73e1 exposes it again.

#### S1-5 · medium · confirmed · risk

**takeTurn treats any refusal as 'busy', ignores JOB_STOP, and its 'turn' outcome is re-run twice as an overlap loss**

- **Where**: `worker.js:14210`, `worker.js:14221`, `worker.js:14222`, `worker.js:14203`, `worker.js:22962`, `worker.js:22963`, `worker.js:6186`, `builder/edit-job.mjs:131`, `worker.js:23129`, `builder/container-job.mjs:197`, `builder/container-job.mjs:202`, `builder/request.mjs:147`, `builder/request.mjs:149`, `builder/request.mjs:1211`, `builder/container-env.mjs:76`
- **What**: The commit fixed the key and left the mechanism. takeTurn catches every tryTurn error, including a GatewayError whose code is 'forbidden', logs 'unreadable' and polls every 3 s. It leaves only on cancelled() or budget.expired(), and in the container the budget is Infinity, so expired() is never true. Only gate() reads env.JOB_STOP, and takeTurn does not, so at the deadline's SIGTERM the job keeps polling until the 20 s belt exits the process: no giveTurn, no refund through its own path, and the lost sweep closes the row. renewTurn returns true on any throw. A job that ends without the turn answers 'turn', which OVERLAP_LOSSES treats as losing to a sibling and re-runs alone twice.
- **What goes wrong**: Any lasting refusal or unreadability of publish-turn/<slug>.json produces the same failure as deploy 2215: the next gateway regression, or a slug that differs from the token's. A container job polls for about 50 minutes, is killed as a process, is refiled once as answerless, and waits again. On the Worker the budget ends it as 'turn', and the driver re-runs that deterministic failure two more times.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:14221 `try { t = await tryTurn(env, slug, owner, job.id); } catch (e) { console.error("publish turn: unreadable for", ...); }` followed by `if (job.budget && typeof job.budget.expired === "function" && job.budget.expired()) return null;`; edit-job.mjs:131 `export const CONTAINER_EDIT_BUDGET_MS = Infinity;`; request.mjs:147 `export const OVERLAP_LOSSES = Object.freeze(["conflict", "turn", "turn-lost", "older"]);`
- **Fix**: In takeTurn and renewTurn, fail at once on `e.code === "forbidden"`, with a refusal code that is not in OVERLAP_LOSSES. Check `env.JOB_STOP.signal.aborted` in the loop, and bound the wait (for example a few TURN_TTL_MS). Report 'turn-unreadable' separately from 'turn' so the driver does not re-run it.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — takeTurn (worker.js:14212-14229) catches every tryTurn throw, including a GatewayError with code 'forbidden' (container-env.mjs:69-77), logs it and polls. It exits only on job.cancelled() or job.budget.expired(). In the container, runContainerJob passes budgetMs=CONTAINER_EDIT_BUDGET_MS=Infinity (worker.js:23129, edit-job.mjs:131) with startedAt=0. inlineBudgetMs then returns Infinity (edit-job.mjs:206-207) and makeEditBudget(Infinity).expired() is never true (edit-job.mjs:447 and :477). env.JOB_STOP is read only by gate() (worker.js:6186), not by takeTurn. So after SIGTERM the loop keeps polling until the 20 s belt exits the process (container-job.mjs:197-203), and the job gives no answer. renewTurn returns true on any throw (worker.js:14203). On the Worker, an unreadable turn ends as error 'turn' (worker.js:22963), which OVERLAP_LOSSES treats as a sibling overlap and re-runs up to OVE…

#### S1-7 · low (raised medium) · confirmed · defect

**A container job cannot read the paused job's own checkpoint, so a part loops in 'recovering' for up to a day when the Worker could not stage it**

- **Where**: `worker.js:21920`, `worker.js:21851`, `worker.js:21891`, `worker.js:21631`, `builder/job-gateway.mjs:439`, `builder/request.mjs:1011`, `builder/request.mjs:1021`, `builder/request.mjs:1430`, `builder/request.mjs:1432`
- **What**: When the staged copy (jobs/prepared/<id>.held-in.json) is missing or stale, readHeldIn falls back to `jobs/prepared/<pausedJob>.held.json`. That key names another job's id, so allowedJobKey (`k.includes(String(id))`) refuses it. tryRead turns the 403 into 'unreadable:Error' (GatewayError is not a logged class), and the route answers checkpoint-unread. stageHeld returns without staging whenever resolveHeld fails ('the job reads it itself'), so in the container that documented recovery never happens.
- **What goes wrong**: A part paused on a question is answered, but the Worker's stageHeld meets a transient read failure and does not stage. The container job returns checkpoint-unread, and the driver marks the part `recovering` with doubling waits up to 30 minutes, for up to 24 hours. It ends only if a later attempt is staged, or as unfinished after WAIT_MS. The customer's answered part does not run.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:21920 `const own = await tryRead(jobHeldKey(want.job));`; job-gateway.mjs:439 `if (k.startsWith("jobs/") && k.includes(String(id))) return true;` (probe: paused job's held key → false); request.mjs:1011 marks only malformed or missing as lost, so 'unreadable' is recovering

### S2 — Seam: request flow ↔ draft-first ↔ publish turn

The request driver (builder/request.mjs `nextStep`) settles each part from its job's row and answer. When `PARALLEL_WRITES=on` (`writeBesideMax`=3, worker.js:13575-13578), it files up to three jobs at once if `clearToWrite` allows. Parts whose run ends with `conflict`/`turn`/`turn-lost`/`older` are re-run as `serial` up to `OVERLAP_RETRIES`=2; answerless jobs and failed routings are retried once (`RETRIES`). Every request job running with the switch on gets `jctx.beside`. Config writers and serial retries (`holdsConfig`) take the site's publish turn (publish-turn/<slug>.json) before their first read and keep it to the end (worker.js:22958). Other jobs take it only inside `publishBeside`, which re-reads the site, rebases the job's own file changes onto it and publishes. Under `DRAFT_FIRST` that publish saves a draft revision (`saveAsDraft`/`saveDraftRecord`); a save behind a newer draft is refused as `older`. `takeTurn` polls every 3 s and stops only on a customer cancel or when the budget expires. In the container the budget is Infinity and the runner's stop signal (`JOB_STOP`) is never checked, so a turn that cannot be read is an unbounded wait while the job's lease keeps the site busy. A stop sets `rec.stop`, cancels every live job through `edit_cancel`, and cancels every part with no job running; the request ends when every part is terminal (`settleState`). The branch's gateway fix admits the turn key and the request record, but the loop that swallowed the 403 is unchanged. The overlap retry also still treats several deterministic, non-overlap failures as overlaps.

#### S2-1 · medium (raised high) · confirmed · defect

**takeTurn treats every error as 'held': in a container a refused or unreadable turn is an unbounded wait that ignores the stop signal and keeps the site busy**

- **Where**: `worker.js:14205-14229`, `worker.js:22876-22887`, `worker.js:22958-22963`, `worker.js:15298-15300`, `worker.js:6186`, `worker.js:23129`, `builder/edit-job.mjs:131`, `builder/edit-job.mjs:206-207`, `builder/container-env.mjs:69-77`, `builder/container-job.mjs:197-203`, `builder/request.mjs:145`, `builder/request.mjs:1052-1059`

A deterministic refusal therefore reads exactly like a turn another job holds. That includes the gateway's typed `GatewayError` with `code: "forbidden"`, which exists precisely so a 401/403 is not mistaken for an outage. The loop ends only when `job.cancelled()` (the customer's cancel, via the heartbeat) or `job.budget.expired()` is true. A container edit runs with `CONTAINER_EDIT_BUDGET_MS = Infinity` and no `startedAt`, so `inlineBudgetMs` returns Infinity and `expired()` is never true (probed: `{ inlineBudgetMs: Infinity, expired: false }`). Unlike `gate()` (worker.js:6186), the loop never reads `env.JOB_STOP`. Throughout the wait the heartbeat keeps renewing the job's lease (22880-22887), so `private.site_busy` refuses every other job on the site. The gateway fix (db4e73e1) removed today's trigger, the 403 on publish-turn/<slug>.json, but not the loop that turned it into a 30-minute stall.
- **What goes wrong**: A job waits for the turn while another job holds it for the rest of the waiter's deadline (a look step holds it from its start), or any gateway call on the turn key keeps failing (a scope regression, a 5xx, a transport failure, a token problem). The waiter polls every 3 s for the whole container deadline (30 minutes in today's live run) and the site stays busy for every other job. At the deadline the runner aborts JOB_STOP, which the loop ignores, and 20 s later the belt exits the process with code 4. The finally block (giveTurn, edit_finalize, refund) never runs, so the lease sweep closes the row with no answer. `answerless` then re-files the part once (RETRIES=1), and the same wait follows. - **Fix**: Make takeTurn fail fast on `e.code === "forbidden"` (and on any non-transient GatewayError), returning a distinct code such as `turn-unreadable` that is not in OVERLAP_LOSSES. Check `env.JOB_STOP.signal.aborted` (or `job.gate()`) on every iteration. Give the wait its own ceiling, finite in the container (for example the turn TTL plus the longest publish), and on timeout end with a named code. Add a gateway-level test where the turn key is refused and the job must end promptly with that code.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — I traced it and the core holds. In worker.js:14219-14228 the takeTurn loop catches every tryTurn throw, logs 'publish turn: unreadable', and polls again. A GatewayError with code 'forbidden' (builder/container-env.mjs:76) is never read anywhere on this path, so a deterministic refusal looks exactly like a turn another job holds. The loop has only two exits: job.cancelled() (set by the heartbeat's edit_beat, worker.js:6157-6165) and job.budget.expired(). #### S2-3 · medium · confirmed · defect

#### S2-5 · low · unverified · gap

**In a container, a resumed part's fallback read of its previous job's checkpoint is outside the gateway's scope**

- **Where**: `worker.js:21915-21928`, `worker.js:21626-21636`, `builder/job-gateway.mjs:437-439`, `builder/request.mjs:1007-1025`
- **What**: `readHeldIn` first reads the copy staged under this job's id. When that is missing or does not match, it falls back to the previous job's own checkpoint, `jobHeldKey(want.job)` = `jobs/prepared/<previousId>.held.json`. The gateway admits a `jobs/` key only if it contains the current job's id. In a container the fallback therefore always fails with a 403 GatewayError, read as `unreadable:GatewayError`. `stageHeld` returns without staging whenever `resolveHeld` fails (21630-21631), and its comment promises the job 'reads it itself'. In the container it never can.
- **What goes wrong**: A part paused on a question; the answer resumes it, but staging fails once (a flaky read in resolveHeld, or the put failing HELD_TRIES times). The container job's fallback is refused with a 403, the job refuses with `checkpoint-unread`, and recoverHeld puts the part in `recovering`, re-run on a doubling backoff. The read the code intends never happens; the part recovers only if a later filing restages, and otherwise waits up to a day.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:21920: `const own = await tryRead(jobHeldKey(want.job));`. builder/job-gateway.mjs:439: `if (k.startsWith("jobs/") && k.includes(String(id))) return true;`.
- **Fix**: Have the Worker always stage the checkpoint (retry staging before filing, or carry it in the job body), or let the gateway admit read-only the checkpoint of a job named on the same request part (as readableJobKey now does for the request record).

#### S2-6 · low · unverified · risk

**With PARALLEL_WRITES on, every editable-state check, including preparations, takes the publish turn and rewrites nine guarded keys, and can fail the owner's Publish**

- **Where**: `worker.js:11804-11806`, `worker.js:13480-13487`, `worker.js:13497-13500`, `worker.js:13851-13877`, `worker.js:20851`, `worker.js:32072-32074`, `worker.js:12990`, `worker.js:13000-13015`, `site-builds.mjs:342-346`, `builder/request.mjs:171-174`
- **What**: `loadSiteSourceForEdit` always calls `ensureEditableState`. With the switch on and no turn named, that takes a `repair:` turn and stamps a fresh fence. Every new turn's gen is larger than any stored, so `stampFences` rewrites the live pointer, head, config, sidecar, source, parts, kit and draft record (same content, new fence bytes, new etags). Worker-side preparations get no `pages` (20851) and read through this path (32072-32074), so a step documented as 'made in the Worker with nothing written to the site' (request.mjs:173-174) takes the publish turn and rewrites live keys. While it holds the turn, publishers wait.
- **What goes wrong**: The owner presses Publish while a request's preparations or jobs are reading the site. runPublication reads the pointer etag (12990) and activates conditionally on it (site-builds.mjs:342-346). A preparation's stamp between the two changes the etag, the activation answers `superseded`, and Publish says 'the site changed while publishing — nothing changed on your live site' (13015), though nothing moved. The window is small but recurs on every read under the switch.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:13480-13486: `if (writesBeside(env) && !turnOwner) { … t = await tryTurn(env, slug, "repair:" + crypto.randomUUID()); … return await ensureEditableState(env, slug, { turnOwner: t.owner, fence: { gen: Number(t.gen) || 0 } }); … }`. worker.js:13866-13876: `if (had === fence.gen) { done = true; break; } … const put = await env.SITES_BUCKET.put(key, fenceBytes(text, fence.gen), { … onlyIf: cond });`.
- **Fix**: Stamp fences only when a repair will actually write, or only for job turns, not read-only checks. Let preparations read without the repairing check. Have runPublication re-read and retry its activation once on `superseded` when the pointer still names `j.from`.

The module header of builder/request.mjs says 'ONE JOB OF A REQUEST IS LIVE AT A TIME'. With PARALLEL_WRITES=on (production since 2026-10-17), nextStep files up to three jobs at once and publishes are serialized by the R2 publish turn instead. The rollout records require `supabase/proposed/request_beside.sql` to be applied before the switch goes on. The repository still lists it under proposed/ 'NOT APPLIED', and its README says applied files move to applied/, so whether production's `site_busy` lets a request's jobs overlap cannot be told from the repo.
- **What goes wrong**: A reader trusting docs/request-flow.md would rule out turn waits, overlap retries and serial re-runs when diagnosing a request, which is exactly today's failure class. If the SQL was not applied, the second and third jobs only defer on `site-busy`, up to 45 deferrals; the switch then buys turn overhead and no parallelism.
- **Evidence**: docs/request-flow.md:38: '**one job of a request runs at a time**, against the site as the part before left it'. worker.js:13577: `const WRITE_BESIDE_MAX = 3;`. supabase/proposed/request_beside.sql:2: '-- PROPOSED — NOT APPLIED.'
- **Fix**: Update docs/request-flow.md and the request.mjs header to describe PARALLEL_WRITES, the publish turn and the overlap retry. Record in the repository whether request_beside.sql was applied, and move it to applied/ with its read-back if it was.

### S3 — Seam: billing ↔ job outcomes

Edits, add-ons and per-part routing jobs are billed through one public.edit_jobs row per job. Each charge is an `edit_reserve`: a debit plus a credit_events row keyed `<job>#<seq>`, idempotent per seq. The publish spine asks `edit_may_publish`, which refuses jobs that are cancelled, under review, terminal or unbilled. `runQueuedSiteEdit` ends every job with `edit_finalize` (reserved→finalized only when published_at is set, or when nothing began publishing and the answer was ok), then calls `edit_refund` for any answer that did not ship. That refund is guarded twice: by the billing state and by credit_events unique(ref,reason). A job whose publish had begun is parked in needs_review for `reconcileEditJob`/`edit_reconcile`. Dead consumers are settled by `edit_sweep_lost`, which refunds them or finalizes a committed job as recovered; queued rows nobody claimed are settled by `edit_sweep_stale`. Approved rewrites (builds) bill outside the row via `credit_debit`/`credit_reverse` on refs `build:<id>:<step>`; `build_debit` is written but still unapplied (supabase/proposed). A message's own routing is debited once per request key (`route:<slug>:<key>`), a part's routing job reserves seq 1 on its own row, and the request driver reads money only from rows (`chargedOf` counts `finalized` only). On every path I traced, money moves exactly once, and the fixture stand-ins mirror the live SQL. The problems are: - unbounded turn waits in the container that hold reserves and lead to a retried deterministic failure; - stops that the data and rules lanes and builds acknowledge but never honour; - container-side limits on the reconcile that is supposed to settle a parked job "at once".

#### S3-1 · medium (raised high) · confirmed · defect

**A container job's wait for the publish turn has no bound and ignores JOB_STOP, so its reserve is held until the process is killed, and the driver then re-runs the same hang**

- **Where**: `worker.js:14210-14229`, `worker.js:15291-15300`, `worker.js:32483-32499`, `worker.js:22954-22966`, `worker.js:6186`, `worker.js:23129`, `builder/edit-job.mjs:131`, `builder/container-job.mjs:197-205`, `builder/request.mjs:145`, `builder/request.mjs:788-797`, `builder/request.mjs:1052-1059`
- **What**: `takeTurn` loops `for (;;)` and returns null only when `job.cancelled()` or `job.budget.expired()`. Every `tryTurn` error is caught, logged and retried (14221-14222). In the container, `runContainerJob` passes `budgetMs: CONTAINER_EDIT_BUDGET_MS` (Infinity), so `makeEditBudget(Infinity).expired()` is always false (probe: `{inline:"Infinity",expired:false}`). The loop never reads `env.JOB_STOP`; only `gate()` does (6186), and takeTurn does not call gate. A job that is not a config writer reaches `publishBeside` → `takeTurn` only after its rungs have reserved (`eCharge` → `edit_reserve`). The job's heartbeat keeps renewing the lease, so neither the lost-job sweep nor the site lock frees anything. At the deadline, SIGTERM aborts JOB_STOP, the loop goes on, and the belt exits 20 s later with no finalize, no refund and no stored answer. The row then waits for the lease to lapse and the lost-job sweep to refund it; with no answer it is `answerless`, so the request files it once more and the same hang repeats. This is today's live class (on main the gateway refuses `publish-turn/<slug>.json`, so every tryTurn throws). The branch admits that key, but the unbounded loop remains for any persistent R2 refusal or a turn held by a long-running holder.
- **What goes wrong**: Production: DRAFT_FIRST=on, PARALLEL_WRITES=on, a text part running in the site's container. The text rung's model call returns and 2 credits are reserved (worker.js:32484). Nothing ends the loop until the deadline SIGTERM (+60 s) and the belt exit (+20 s), about 51 minutes. The 2 credits stay debited until the 90 s lease, the 60 s grace and the next 2-minute sweep; the row ends `lost` with no answer. The driver re-files it (RETRIES=1) and the hang and the hold repeat, then the part fails `no-answer`. Stop retrying a tryTurn error that is a typed refusal (code `forbidden`); answer it at once as an ours-side refusal. Consider taking the turn before the first reserve for every request job under PARALLEL_WRITES, so no wait ever holds money. Classify a forbidden-key refusal as non-retryable in the request driver.

#### S3-2 · medium · confirmed · gap

**The data and rules lanes never honour a Stop: edit_cancel says `cancel: true`, then the change is applied and the reserve finalized**

- **Where**: `worker.js:33648`, `worker.js:33986`, `worker.js:36969-36991`, `worker.js:22425-22446`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:70-93`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:95-162`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:246-277`, `worker.js:38384-38403`
- **What**: Five places in all of worker.js check a cancel through `gate()`: the routing start, the edit route's pre-publish gate (36987), and three add-on gates. The edit route's single gate sits inside `if (pendingPublish && ...)`, and a data or rules change has nothing to publish (36969: 'A CHANGE WITH NOTHING TO PUBLISH (a row, a rule)'). Their `before` callbacks reserve and then return `!(eCharges.refused() > 0)` without asking `eJob.gate()` or `cancelled()`. These lanes never call `edit_may_publish` or `edit_committed`, so published_at stays null and `edit_cancel` keeps answering `{ok:true, cancel:true}`, even after the row write committed. `edit_finalize` has no cancel check, and `edit_claim` has none either, so a part stopped while still queued is claimed and runs to the end. stopRequest's contract ("stopped before it publishes, or answered too-late after") is therefore false for these lanes. The add-on row step closed exactly this hole by gating its write on `edit_may_publish` (`aRowGate`), but the edit route's data lane did not get the same gate.
- **What goes wrong**: A request has a data part ('change the Lessons price to £40') and a second part. The stop changed nothing for this part, yet the customer was told it was accepted and was charged. The same timing on a text or look part would have been refused at `edit_may_publish` and refunded.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:33648: `before: async (usage) => { if (isPrep) {...} dCost = await eCharge(usage); dBilled = true; return !(eCharges.refused() > 0); }` (rules lane identical at 33986). `grep -n "\.gate(" worker.js` → 30140, 36987, 40287, 40728, 41387 only. edit_cancel (snapshot :86-91): it answers 'too-late' only when published_at is set, otherwise it sets cancel_requested_at and returns cancel true. The edit_claim UPDATE (snapshot :137-146) has no cancel_requested_at predicate.
- **Fix**: In the data and rules lanes' `before` callbacks, ask `eJob.gate("apply")` after the reserve and before the first write; on `go:false` return through `editStopped` (which refunds). Better still, gate the write through `edit_may_publish` and record it with `edit_committed`, as the add-on row step does, so the cancel and the lost-job sweep are both enforced by the ledger. Alternatively, have `edit_claim` refuse rows with cancel_requested_at set.

It never reaches the edit route's only pre-publish gate (36987), which in any case sits inside if(pendingPublish ...) #### S3-3 · medium · confirmed · risk · already recorded

**A request rewrite filed in the container debits through the customer's stored bearer, so a deferred rewrite fails its deposit, or its settle and page debits, once the token expires**

- **Where**: `worker.js:610-650`, `worker.js:24727-24740`, `worker.js:22480-22489`, `builder/job-gateway.mjs:136-140`, `supabase/proposed/README.md`, `builder/edit-job.mjs:355`
- **What**: An approved rewrite is packed with the press's Authorization header (rewriteJob). In the container, `buildLedger.debit` first calls `build_debit` through the gateway. PostgREST answers 404 (the SQL is not applied), so `absent=true` and the fallback presents the stored bearer to `credit_debit`. A 401 from an expired token is then re-thrown, because `absent` is true. The build route answers 503 'Credits check failed — try again in a moment.', and the rewrite part fails with no charge and no way to retry short of a new approval. If the token instead expires mid-build, the settle and page debits fail and the rewrite is saved for free (backlog H2).

- **Fix**: Apply supabase/proposed/build_debit.sql (the owner's decision), so container builds bill the row's account under the mint key. Until then, have the request driver re-file a rewrite that failed on a refused bearer, using a fresh session.
- **Already recorded**: docs/backlog.md:291-296 (build_debit.sql must be applied; H2)
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — rewriteJob (worker.js:22480-22489) packs the press's auth into the rewrite's job. buildLedger.debit (606-650) tries build_debit first. On a 404, absent=true (619), and the fallback presents the bearer to credit_debit. A 401/403 is re-thrown when absent is true (642-644, and again at 646 after the second build_debit 404). build_debit exists only in supabase/proposed/build_debit.sql; nothing under supabase/applied defines it. The build route's deposit catch (24731-24739) reverses by ref and answers 503 'Credits check failed'. Later settle or pages debits that fail let the rewrite through unbilled, which is the documented H2 shape. The request flow's deferral only lengthens the token's age; the mechanism is the documented limit. #### S3-5 · low · unverified · risk

**In the container, the immediate reconcile after a post-gate refusal can never reach a non-draft verdict, so the reserve stays held and the site is closed to new jobs until the Worker's review sweep**

- **Where**: `builder/container-env.mjs:24`, `worker.js:20108`, `builder/site-reconcile.mjs:235`, `worker.js:23074-23080`, `worker.js:20326-20330`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:213`, `worker.js:22066-22073`
- **What**: `reconcileAfterRefund` runs inside runQueuedSiteEdit, in the container for container jobs. `reconcileFacts` probes the live script only when `env.SITE_WORKERS` exists, and the container env deliberately lacks it. Every staged-but-unsaved case (a post-gate turn loss, an activation or draft-write failure) therefore falls to `if (!live) return answer("unknown", "live-unreadable", ...)`, and the row stays needs_review with billing still reserved. Meanwhile `edit_create` refuses every new job on the site ('needs-review'), including the part's own overlap re-run and the other parts' filings, until `runReviewReconcile` in the Worker decides it on a later tick. The code comment promises a reconcile 'at once' because 'the facts are freshest here'.
- **What goes wrong**: PARALLEL_WRITES=on. A container job loses its turn inside the fenced activation after `edit_may_publish` granted it. edit_refund → needs-review, and the in-container reconcile answers unknown/live-unreadable. For the next 2+ minutes the customer's reserve is held and every filing for the site is refused (`noteFilingRefused` → 'site-review'). The Worker sweep then refunds it as never-activated, and only after that does the overlap re-run start.
- **Evidence**: builder/container-env.mjs:24: '// SITE_API_CACHE, EMAIL, SITE_WORKERS, ASSETS — not on the job path; absent.' worker.js:20108: `const live = env.SITE_WORKERS ? await probeSiteWorker(...) : null;`. builder/site-reconcile.mjs:235: `if (!live) return answer("unknown", "live-unreadable", ...)`.
- **Fix**: Hand an unknown verdict from a container job to the Worker at once: wake the review reconcile through the gateway (as `/next` wakes the driver), or answer the job's end to the Worker so it reconciles with SITE_WORKERS. Alternatively, under draft-first, treat 'staged, not in the draft, pointer not ours' as never-activated without needing the live probe.

#### S3-6 · low · unverified · defect

**Reconcile treats a held-only draft revision as proof that the whole job was saved, so a job whose page publish failed after the gate is charged in full and its reply is replaced with 'saved as a draft'**

- **Where**: `builder/site-reconcile.mjs:163-185`, `worker.js:33744-33752`, `worker.js:36987-37001`, `worker.js:20184-20235`
- **What**: The data lane seals held rows into their own draft revision naming the job (sealHeld, 33745), then defers its reorder publish through `publishStep`, which ships at the end of the job behind `edit_may_publish`. If that final publish fails after the gate, edit_refund parks the job. `draftVerdict` accepts any revision of this job that carries held changes ('a held-only seal … its held changes were saved') and answers kept/draft-saved. `edit_reconcile(p_committed)` then finalizes the whole reserve, and `applyReconcile` overwrites the job's failure answer with a recovered 'saved as draft' reply.
- **What goes wrong**: Draft-first on a live site: 'set Lessons row 4 to £40 and list lessons by price'. The rows are held into revision N; the reorder publish is refused after the gate (for example, a fenced draft write refused under PARALLEL_WRITES). Reconcile finds revision N → kept. The customer is charged for the reorder too, and the reply says the change was saved as draft revision N, although the new order is not in the draft.
- **Evidence**: builder/site-reconcile.mjs:170-172: `if (m.state === "read") { const theirs = !(m.manifest && m.manifest.job === job.id); if (!theirs || x.held) { r = x; break; } ... }` → :183 `answer("kept", "draft-saved", ...)`. worker.js:20226: a kept verdict with a non-ok prior is re-finalized with `reconcileReply(...)` and p_ok true.
- **Fix**: When the job also staged its own version (`mine`) and that version is absent from the draft, answer `partial` or unknown instead of `kept`. Or keep the held seal and the page publish in one revision (pass `held` into activateBuild, as the page path already does), so one verdict covers both.

#### S3-7 · low · unverified · defect

**A failed editable-state check is reported as error "turn", so the request driver re-runs a non-overlap failure as an overlap loss**

- **Where**: `worker.js:22954-22966`, `builder/request.mjs:147`, `builder/request.mjs:1206-1218`
- **What**: For a step that holds the turn throughout, runQueuedSiteEdit answers `{ ok:false, error:"turn", ... }` both when the turn could not be taken and when `ensureEditableState` failed (`heldSt.ok !== true`, e.g. why 'repair', meaning the repair or config write failed). "turn" is in OVERLAP_LOSSES, so the driver re-runs the part serially up to OVERLAP_RETRIES=2 more times, each a new job that waits for the turn again. A deterministic repair failure (an R2 or gateway refusal of a key the repair writes) is retried three times and then fails as a turn loss.
- **What goes wrong**: A config-writing part is in a container where the editable-state repair cannot write one key. Each attempt takes the turn, the repair fails, and the job answers error 'turn' with the 'Couldn't check the site's saved state' message. The driver re-runs it twice more and the part then fails, with no money moved and three wasted job slots and turn holds.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:22963-22964: `if (jctx.beside && jctx.beside.holds && (!jctx.beside.turn || !heldSt || heldSt.ok !== true)) { res = Response.json({ ok: false, error: "turn", ours: true, cost: 0, unchanged: true, msg: heldSt && !jctx.beside.lost ? "Couldn't check the site's saved state before this change. Nothing was changed." : ... }`. builder/request.mjs:147: `OVERLAP_LOSSES = ["conflict", "turn", "turn-lost", "older"]`.
- **Fix**: Answer a failed editable-state check with its own code (e.g. `read` or `editable-state`, as publishBeside already does at worker.js:15308), and keep "turn" only for a turn that was genuinely not obtained.

#### S3-8 · low · unverified · doc-drift

**The edit 'no-container' path leaves the row claimed (not terminal) and does not tell the request, despite its comment**

- **Where**: `worker.js:1666-1677`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:258-268`
- **What**: When the container cannot take an edit after FIRE_RETRY_MAX tries, the consumer calls only `edit_finalize(p_ok:false)`. With published_at null and p_ok false, edit_finalize stores the result and changes nothing else, so the row stays `claimed` under the consumer's 90 s lease. The comment says 'the row is terminal, and the poll stops rather than spinning'. Nothing is refunded or ended until the lost-job sweep, and `requestJobEnded` is not called, so the request moves on only at the next request sweep. No money is at stake (nothing was reserved).
- **What goes wrong**: The container is out of room for about 6 s of fire retries. The row stays `claimed`, the site counts as busy to other jobs, and the page keeps polling a running job for about 3.5 minutes (90 s lease, 60 s grace, then the next 2-minute tick). Only then does the row become `lost`, the stored 'no-container' answer is served, and the request's retry is filed.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:1667-1676: '// … the customer is told, the row is terminal, and the poll stops rather than spinning.' followed only by `await editRpc(env, "edit_finalize", { p_id: edit.id, p_ok: false, p_result: {...} })`. edit_finalize's state update needs `published_at is not null or (publish_started_at is null and coalesce(p_ok,false))`.
- **Fix**: Follow the finalize with `edit_refund(p_state:'failed', note 'no container')`, as `deferEditJob`'s give-up already relies on the claim's own refund, then call `requestJobEnded`. Do the same on the build path at worker.js:18899-18906.

#### S3-9 · low · unverified · defect

**edit_refund overwrites the state of a row that is already terminal: a routing job's own cancel is recorded as `failed`**

- **Where**: `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:436-478`, `worker.js:30138-30144`, `worker.js:23063-23074`
- **What**: edit_refund refuses only `done` rows; for cancelled, failed or lost rows with no reserve it runs `update ... set state = p_state`. The routing handler's gate calls `edit_refund(p_state:'cancelled')`, then the consumer's generic end calls `edit_refund(p_state:'failed', 'edit did not ship')` on the same row, flipping it cancelled→failed. A late consumer likewise rewrites a sweep's `lost`. Money is safe (the billing guard), but the row's terminal state no longer says how the job ended. Only the stored answer's `error: "cancelled"` keeps `settle()` correct.
- **What goes wrong**: A request is stopped while a part's routing job waits. The job ends cancelled at its gate, then the consumer's own refund turns the row into `failed`. Anything reading row.state (the poll route's `ok: row.state !== "failed"`, phase statistics, `wantsEvidence`) sees a failure instead of a cancellation.
- **Evidence**: snapshot :475: `update public.edit_jobs set state = p_state, updated_at = now() where id = p_id;` is reached for any non-done row without a reserve. worker.js:30142 `edit_refund(... p_state: rGate.why === "cancelled" ? "cancelled" : "failed" ...)` is followed by worker.js:23072 `edit_refund(... p_state: "failed", p_note: "edit did not ship")`.
- **Fix**: In edit_refund, return `{ok:true, refunded:0, state}` unchanged for a row already in ('failed','cancelled','lost') (a migration and the owner's decision). Or skip the consumer's second refund when the answer already says it ended at a gate.

#### S3-10 · low · unverified · doc-drift

**The backlog says edit_claim refuses a job whose cancel was requested, but the live function has no such check**

- **Where**: `docs/backlog.md:1745-1748`, `supabase/applied/20260901222000_live_snapshot_edit_rpcs.sql:95-162`
- **What**: docs/backlog.md (MR5) states '`edit_claim` refuses a job whose cancel was requested and the consumer only logs it'. edit_claim's pre-checks and its UPDATE test needs_review, the terminal state, billing and the lease, never cancel_requested_at. A Stop pressed before the claim is enforced only by the job's own gates, and the data and rules lanes have none (S3-2).
- **What goes wrong**: Someone reasoning from the backlog assumes a queued part stopped before its claim never runs. In fact it is claimed and run, and a data or rules part applies its change and keeps its reserve.
- **Evidence**: snapshot :110-117: `if j.needs_review or j.state in ('done','failed','cancelled','lost') or j.billing in ('finalized','refunded') or (j.lease_owner is not null and j.lease_expires_at >= now()) then ... end if;`. No cancel_requested_at appears anywhere in edit_claim.
- **Fix**: Correct the backlog line. If refusing cancelled claims is wanted, add `cancel_requested_at is null` to edit_claim and settle such a row through edit_refund('cancelled').

### S4 — Seam: Publish ↔ media ↔ data held changes ↔ restore

Under DRAFT_FIRST, a task on a live site does not write the database or library. It holds those changes in an immutable journal (site-draft.mjs newHold/sealHeldRevision; worker.js backendWriter, heldDeleteOr, and the held media-replace route at 44368-44425). Each journal is named by a numbered revision in site-drafts/<slug>.json. Publish (worker.js publishDraft → runPublication, 12892-13124) reads the held ops of (applied, n] and folds them with publishPlan. The order is: latest schema, latest jobs, seeds, row changes, inserts, library. It then runs a phase journal: prepare (new tables and their seeds), switching (pointer, staged sidecar, script), and switched (address, schema, jobs, seeds, changes, inserts, library). It finishes with markApplied. The 2-minute tick (runPublishRecovery) finishes a switched journal with no attempt cap, and clickPlan makes every later click finish it first. The preview serves /u/ and /api/db by overlaying the unpublished ops (servePreview 13328-13392). Versions restore (restoreVersion) activates any staged build directly, and the media sweep reclaims sessions, parts and pre-site drafts, never uploads/. Everything here runs in the Worker except held-op creation and pre-site media adoption, which run in container jobs through the job gateway. No live run of held publication exists yet: the rollout checklist §7 batch is prepared but nothing has been pressed.

No live run: docs/history/2026-10-16-rollout-checklist.md §7 is prepared and docs/owner-notes.md 2026-10-17 says nothing runs until authorized. |

#### S4-2 · high · confirmed · defect

**A held row change the database refuses deterministically leaves the publication 'switched' forever, retried every 2 minutes, and blocks every later Publish**

The bad op also sits in every later revision's range. The panel shows only 'Finish publishing — it is also retried automatically'. The library step comes last, so held media replacements and removals in the same revision are never applied. The sweep scans from the start of the prefix with `max = 10`, so ten such journals starve recovery for every site whose key sorts after them. docs/history/2026-10-15-draft-first.md §7.6/§8.5 acknowledges only that a step whose store keeps refusing is unbounded. Each later 'Publish this draft' runs finishFirst and fails the same way, and the replaced hero video in that revision never goes live.

- **Fix**: Classify finish-step errors with rowWriteOutcome. On a definite refusal (classes 22/23/42), mark the journal failed-with-cause and stop automatic retries. Cap or back off the sweep, and walk it with a cursor so stuck journals cannot starve other sites.

#### S4-7 · medium · confirmed · defect

**Publish writes the draft version's staged sidecar whole, reverting head changes made since it was staged**

- **Where**: `worker.js:12994-12995`, `worker.js:13022`, `worker.js:12867-12879`, `worker.js:14618-14627`, `worker.js:16100-16113`, `worker.js:17442-17444`, `worker.js:44005-44010`, `worker.js:44112`, `worker.js:44222`
- **What**: A version's sidecar (origin, description, share image, verification tags) is composed when the version is staged: publicUrlFor and the stored verify, image and description at that moment. Owner panels such as Verify, Share and SEO act at once by patching the live sidecar and config. Under draft-first, Publish activates a version staged earlier and writes `b.sidecar` whole (completeActivation writes it whenever the text differs). Only a held rename in the same plan overrides `origin`. So any panel change made between staging and Publish is reverted at Publish. A held rename is also reverted when the version published next was staged before the rename's publication. That happens when a job saves a later revision while the owner publishes the earlier one; the panel says 'publishing now releases only the draft below'.
- **What goes wrong**: An owner makes edits (saved as drafts), then pastes a Google Search Console token in Verify. It goes live at once and Google verifies. The next day they press Publish. The draft version's staged sidecar has no verify pairs, so the tag disappears from the live head and Search Console verification lapses. Rename case: revision 1 is a held rename A→B; a running edit stages V2 (origin A) while the owner publishes revision 1 (origin B). When the owner later publishes revision 2, the canonical and og:url revert to A.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:12994 `let sidecar = typeof b.sidecar === "string" ? b.sidecar : undefined; if (rename && sidecar) { … sd.origin = addressOf(rename.to); … }`. worker.js:12872-12876 writes `sidecar` when `text !== sidecar`. worker.js:16107 `url: await publicUrlFor(env, slug)` at staging. Panels: 44008 `side.verify = …`, 44112 `side.image = …`, 44222 `side.description = …`, each written to the live sidecar only.
- **Fix**: At Publish, re-compose the head from the current stored config and the post-publication public name, or merge the live sidecar's owner-panel fields (verify, image, description, origin) over the staged one, and keep only the version's own routes and redirects.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — The sidecar is composed when the version is staged, from the stored verify, description, image and publicUrlFor at that moment (worker.js:16100-16113, 17442-17444, composePublish 14618-14627). At Publish, runPublication passes the staged `b.sidecar` and overrides only `origin`, and only for a held rename in the same plan (12994-12995). completeActivation writes it whenever its text differs from the live one (12867-12879). The Verify (44005-44010), Share (44108-44112) and SEO (44218-44222) panels patch only the live sidecar. Nothing re-merges verify at Publish: verificationPairs is written only at 14627 and 44008. So a panel change made between staging and Publish is reverted, which under draft-first can be days. Before draft-first the gap was seconds. The backlog's preview item notes the rename address in the preview, not this revert.

#### S4-8 · medium · confirmed · defect

- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — servePreview (worker.js:13343-13347) resolves held library ops with one `file` variable. After a media-replace it follows `with`, so later ops naming the original address no longer match, while ops naming the stand-in do. applyHeldMedia (13286-13311) applies the ops in sequence: copy `with`→`name`, delete `with`; media-delete deletes `name`. The held-replace route (44381-44392) checks only that the live object exists and its asset is not 'deleted'. A held replacement or held removal does not change that, so a second replace, or a replace then a delete, of the same file is allowed. The Files list marks only stand-ins and removals (44283-44296), so the original file still shows normally. Traced by hand: replace twice previews the first replacement and goes live with the second. Replace then delete plays in the preview and is 404 live. Deleting the stand-in is 404 in the preview and plays …

#### S4-10 · low · unverified · defect

**Publish records held library changes as done when they were not applied (a 4xx from the delete, or a missing stand-in)**

- **Where**: `worker.js:12952-12954`, `worker.js:13287-13298`, `worker.js:13300-13303`
- **What**: applyHeldMedia treats any answer under 500 from handleMediaDelete as success, including 409 `replacing` (a fresh claim on the file), so a held removal can be marked applied while the file stays. The preflight allows a replacement whose stand-in is gone as long as the original exists (`!head(with) && !head(name)`). The finish then treats a missing `src` as already done, so the replacement silently does not happen. The preview, meanwhile, showed 404 for the stand-in's address.
- **What goes wrong**: The site is taken offline (no pointer), so siteIsLive is false and a delete goes direct. The owner deletes the stand-in, brings the site back online and publishes. The preflight passes on the original, `src` is null, and the step returns ok. Publish reports success with the old bytes still live.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:12953 `if (m.kind === "media-replace" && !(await …head(uploadKey(slug, m.with))) && !(await …head(uploadKey(slug, m.name)))) return before(…)`. worker.js:13288 `if (src) { … }` followed by `return { ok: true };`. worker.js:13302 `if (del && del.status && del.status >= 500) return { ok: false, … }`.
- **Fix**: Require the stand-in at preflight unless the journal shows the step was already done. Treat 409 `replacing` and other non-404 4xx answers as not done, and keep the journal.

### S5 — Seam: browser app ↔ server contracts

The page (public/chat.js with the testable helpers public/edit-poll.js and public/site-media.js) reads server answers in six places. (1) `GET /api/site/<slug>/draft` (worker.js:43190-43230) returns draftState() from site-draft.mjs:321-339 plus preview, previewState/previewReady, publication and address. The page uses it to paint the chip, to point the frame at the `<slug>--draft-<token>` host (chat.js:5258-5279), and to keep re-reading on a 5 s to 2 min backoff (chat.js:8048-8097). (2) `POST …/publish` takes `{revision, version}` and answers ok/already, or 202 publishing, 409 or 503 with `live`; the panel (chat.js:8110-8183) reads every one of those fields. (3) `GET /api/site/request/<slug>/<key>` returns requestView (builder/request.mjs:2197-2277). The card maps each part's status, prep, needs, why and draft to labels (chat.js:10933-11030), and every part's job is read through `GET /api/site/edit/<job>` (worker.js:30710-30818) and told by editReply or addonReplyText. (4) Media goes up in parts through site-media.js against site-media.mjs, with draft-first pairing for replacements in worker.js:44370-44425. (5) The Files list shows the `draft: remove|replaces` marks. (6) The `draftFirst` flag comes from /api/credits. Field names and types match between the two sides; I found no renamed or missing field. The problems are in meaning: fixed sentences and one media path that are not draft-aware, and draft states that leave out work the server knows about. The draft and media seam is proven offline only (in-process real Worker, supplied model answers). The rollout checklist §8 lists it as unverified live.

### S6 — Seam: switch matrix

Each switch has its own reader in the Worker, and the readers accept different spellings. requestFlowOn, editAsyncOn and jobRunnerFor take 1/true/on/yes. writesBeside, repliesOn and progressOn/talkOn take only "on" (trimmed). draftFirst takes only "on" and does not trim. imagePurchasesOn treats anything except "off" as on. deploy.yml sets every switch as a Worker secret with a fallback when unset. A container job sees only JOB_ENV_NAMES (edit-job.mjs:1016-1064): DRAFT_FIRST, PARALLEL_WRITES, MODEL_REPLIES, PROGRESS_*, IMAGE_PURCHASES and EDIT_ASYNC* are on the list. REQUEST_FLOW and JOB_RUNNER_* are not, which is correct because only the Worker reads them. A container job reaches R2 and Supabase only through the job gateway's allowlist. With REQUEST_FLOW on (and edits queued), the Worker's advanceRequest files each part's job. PARALLEL_WRITES lets it file up to 3 at once; each such job takes publish-turn/<slug>.json, from its first read when it holds config or only at publish otherwise, and fences its guarded writes. Every edit or add-on start also takes a brief "repair" turn and re-stamps the site's guarded objects. With DRAFT_FIRST on, every Build, Edit and Add-on saves a draft revision. Only the owner's Publish moves the live site, and Publish runs in the Worker without taking the turn. The branch's gateway fix admits the turn key and the request record. Still left: pre-site media is refused by the gateway in container builds; the model-written replies drop the draft fact for held changes; and the turn wait treats a refusal as transient and then re-runs it as an overlap loss. The combination production runs now (DRAFT_FIRST + PARALLEL_WRITES + REQUEST_FLOW + container runner through the gateway) is tested only one job at a time (DH6). Overlapping container jobs were run only against the bucket directly (PPM2) or inline in the Worker (CW1-CW5), with MODEL_REPLIES off and IMAGE_PURCHASES on, the opposite of production.

| What it does | Shown | Evidence |

The deploy-2215 live run where container jobs tried the turn (so they read PARALLEL_WRITES on) is recorded only in commit db4e73e1's message, not in owner-notes, history or the checklist. |
| REQUEST_FLOW: the server finishes a request's part through EDIT_ASYNC, the container runner and MODEL_REPLIES (DRAFT_FIRST and PARALLEL_WRITES off) | live-proven | docs/history/2026-10-04-request-batch.md §1, run 94 (rq-canary): request 03e48000… ended done, its job ran in a cold container, the page posted no edit, and the reply was model-written. |
| A container request job takes the publish turn through the real gateway | offline-only | DH6 (test/draft-handoff.test.mjs:286) runs through the gateway but one job at a time. On production main the same path failed live (commit db4e73e1: both jobs waited 30 minutes). |
| Two container jobs of one request overlapping through the gateway (the combination production runs) | untested | PPM2 (test/parallel-publish-media.test.mjs:265) overlaps but calls containerEnvOf without `worker`, so it uses the platform bucket directly. DH6 awaits each launch and has no `beside` lock mirror. CW1-CW5 (test/concurrent-writes.test.mjs) run inline in the Worker. |

#### S6-3 · medium · confirmed · risk

**The turn wait treats a gateway refusal as transient, and its 'turn' failure is re-run twice as an overlap loss that again holds the turn from the start**

- **Where**: `worker.js:14210-14229`, `builder/container-env.mjs:69-78`, `worker.js:22894-22902`, `worker.js:22957-22963`, `worker.js:13471-13540`, `builder/request.mjs:147-149`, `builder/request.mjs:1211-1217`, `builder/request-plan.mjs:616`
- **What**: takeTurn catches every tryTurn error, logs it and polls every 3 s until the job's budget expires (14221-14228). It never checks GatewayError.code === 'forbidden', which the shim sets for 401/403 precisely because 'nothing a retry fixes'. Two different failures both come back as `error: "turn"` (22962-22963): the wait running out, and the turn obtained but ensureEditableState returning ok:false (draft unreadable, pointer unreadable, fence stamp failed, repair failed). "turn" is in OVERLAP_LOSSES, so nextStep re-runs the part up to OVERLAP_RETRIES=2 times with `serial` set. holdsConfig is true for a serial part (request-plan.mjs:616), so each re-run waits for the turn from its first read again. A part whose request record cannot be read also holds the turn (22895-22902). The gateway fix removes the one known refusal, but this loop and classification are unchanged, so any later scope gap or deterministic store fault repeats the 3 × budget pattern.
- **What goes wrong**: Two cases. (1) A future gateway or scope regression on publish-turn/ or the request record: each container request job polls about 1,000 times over its whole budget. The part fails 'turn', is re-run alone twice, waits the whole budget each time, and only then fails. The message says 'Another change in this request is still being published', which is false. This is the live failure as it happened on deploy 2215. (2) A malformed site-drafts/<slug>.json (readDraft throws 'draft unreadable'): every config-holding part fails 'turn' immediately, is re-run twice deterministically, and then fails.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:14220-14228: `try { t = await tryTurn(env, slug, owner, job.id); } catch (e) { console.error("publish turn: unreadable for", …); } … await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, turnPollMs(env)));`. container-env.mjs:77: `this.code = this.status === 403 || this.status === 401 ? "forbidden" : "transient";`. request.mjs:147: `OVERLAP_LOSSES = ["conflict", "turn", "turn-lost", "older"]`. request-plan.mjs:616: `holdsConfig(part) … (writesConfig(part) || part.serial === true)`.
- **Fix**: In takeTurn, stop at once on a GatewayError with code 'forbidden' (or any non-transient code) and return a distinct error such as 'turn-unreadable'. Give ensureEditableState failures their own error code (for example 'editable-state'). Leave both out of OVERLAP_LOSSES so they fail once with the true reason.
- **Check (batch)**: confirmed, medium — The code is as described. takeTurn (worker.js:14211-14229) catches every tryTurn error, logs it (14222) and keeps polling every turnPollMs (3000 ms default, publish-turn.mjs:31). It stops only when the job is cancelled or its budget expires. It never looks at GatewayError.code, which is 'forbidden' for 401/403 (container-env.mjs:77). The job runner returns `error: "turn"` for two different cases (worker.js:22957-22963): no turn obtained, and the turn held but ensureEditableState returning ok:false (draft unreadable 13509-13512, pointer 13503-13504, fence stamp 13495-13498, repair 13560-13563). readDraft throws 'draft unreadable' on a malformed record (site-draft.mjs:44-52). readRun classifies any ok:false as a refusal (request.mjs:591). #### S6-4 · medium · confirmed · untested

**No test runs two container jobs of one request overlapping through the real gateway, which is the combination production now runs**

- **Where**: `test/draft-handoff.test.mjs:142-160`, `test/draft-handoff.test.mjs:177-195`, `test/draft-handoff.test.mjs:286`, `test/fixtures/request-flow.mjs:288-293`, `test/fixtures/request-flow.mjs:788`, `test/parallel-publish-media.test.mjs:226`, `test/parallel-publish-media.test.mjs:258-267`, `test/fixtures/fired-jobs.mjs:30-35`, `test/concurrent-writes.test.mjs:20-25`
- **What**: DH6 is the regression test for the live failure, and its title says the two jobs 'run in the container beside each other'. But firedBakery builds the platform without `beside: true`, so the fixture's site lock is the applied one (request-flow.mjs:289-293) and same-request jobs block each other. drive() also awaits each launch in turn (draft-handoff:181-190), so the jobs never overlap. PPM2 does overlap container jobs, but it calls `containerEnvOf(P.env, l.body)` without `worker`, so the jobs hold the platform bucket directly instead of the gateway (fired-jobs.mjs:30-34). CW1-CW5 run inline in the Worker. As a result, the fenced writes as they travel through the gateway (head(), the fence in x-gf-meta, x-gf-if-match/none-match), concurrent tryTurn and renewTurn, and stampFences racing between two container jobs are never exercised together. #### S6-6 · low · unverified · risk

**With PARALLEL_WRITES on, every edit or add-on start re-stamps the live pointer, live marker and sidecar, while the owner's Publish runs outside the turn and switches on the pointer etag it read**

- **Where**: `worker.js:11804-11816`, `worker.js:13481-13499`, `worker.js:13829-13880`, `worker.js:12986-13015`, `worker.js:12867-12878`, `site-builds.mjs:342-346`
- **What**: loadSiteSourceForEdit runs at the start of the edit route, the add-on route, a revise, the platform rebuild, the owner's text editor and Back online. It calls ensureEditableState with no turnOwner. When writesBeside is on, that takes a 'repair:' turn and recurses with a fence (13481-13486), and stampFences then rewrites every guarded key with the new fence bytes, including current/<slug>.json, sites/<slug>/<live file> and sitemeta/<slug>.json, each with a new etag. The owner's Publish (runPublication) does not take the turn. It reads the pointer tag (12990) and activates with `etagMatches` on it (site-builds.mjs:342-346). Separately, completeActivation writes the sidecar conditionally on the sidecar it read (12876).
- **What goes wrong**: Draft-first explicitly allows Publish while request jobs are still running. If a job start's stamp lands between Publish's pointer read and its pointer write, activateBuild answers 'superseded'. Publish then retires with 'the site changed while publishing — nothing changed on your live site', although nothing changed. If the stamp lands on the sidecar step instead, the journal is kept 'unknown' with the new version live on the old sidecar until the recovery sweep runs. The window is short, a single R2 write.
- **Evidence**: worker.js:13481-13485: `if (writesBeside(env) && !turnOwner) { … t = await tryTurn(env, slug, "repair:" + crypto.randomUUID()); … return await ensureEditableState(env, slug, { turnOwner: t.owner, fence: { gen: Number(t.gen) || 0 } }); }`. worker.js:13851 is the stamp list (POINTER, HEAD, CONFIG, sitemeta, LIVE, SOURCE, PARTS, KIT, DRAFT). site-builds.mjs:345-346: `const moved = await deps.put(POINTER_KEY(slug), …, onlyIf); if (moved === null) return { ok: false, error: "superseded" };`.
- **Fix**: Either have Publish take the site's turn (and fence its writes) when writesBeside is on, or make the repair-turn stamp skip the live-serving keys (pointer, live marker, sidecar) when no repair is needed. On 'superseded', have Publish re-read the pointer and retry once when the version and parent are unchanged.

#### S6-8 · low · unverified · risk

### S7 — Seam: recovery ↔ live state

The two-minute cron (worker.js:1470-1535) runs about 15 sweeps inside one scheduled invocation. The ones that act on live state are: runLostEditJobs (the SQL edit_sweep_lost and edit_sweep_stale, then runReviewReconcile, which uses builder/site-reconcile.mjs and under draft-first decides first from the job's own draft revision); runRequestSweep (advanceRequest/nextStep re-file parts, including the bounded 're-run alone after an overlap'); runScriptPendingSweep (puts the live script back on the pointer after a dead uploader); runMediaSweep (sessions, parts and pre-site drafts only; never uploads/, so held replacements' stand-ins are left alone); runPreviewRecovery (per-writer claims, waits 16 minutes, then converges the preview to the draft); and runPublishRecovery (resumes a publication journal or sets it aside once it is 3 minutes stale). Live jobs are protected by a 90-second lease renewed every 30 seconds (edit_beat) and by a 300-second publish lease from edit_may_publish. With PARALLEL_WRITES on, a per-site publish turn is added (10-minute TTL, renewed on the beat), and its generation is stamped into nine guarded keys. A draft save writes its preview claim before its record and commits only after converging the preview. The weak seams follow one pattern. A liveness signal is time-based, but the live work contains a longer single wait: the publication journal goes 3 minutes without a write while a script upload can wait 10. Some waits have no bound in the container: takeTurn, because CONTAINER_EDIT_BUDGET_MS is Infinity. A refusal code is shared by non-overlap causes, so the request driver retries deterministic failures. A 'turn held' answer is read as 'nothing to repair'. Almost all draft-first recovery behaviour is offline-only, and the first live parallel request failed at the gateway's turn refusal.

#### S7-2 · medium (raised high) · confirmed · defect

**Turn waits have no bound in the container, and every failure to get the turn is re-run as an 'overlap'**

- **What**: The gateway fix removes the trigger seen live, but the two mechanisms that turned it into a 30-minute hang retried 3 times remain on the branch. (1) takeTurn retries an unreadable turn every 3 s and stops only on job.cancelled() or job.budget.expired(). In the container the budget is makeEditBudget(Infinity), so expired() is never true. takeTurn also ignores env.JOB_STOP, which gate() checks first. The wait ends only on a cancel, or on the kill at the 50-minute deadline, which leaves no answer: the row goes lost, the part is read as answerless, and it runs once more. (2) Every failure to get or verify the turn is answered `error: "turn"`. That covers an unreadable or refused turn store, ensureEditableState failing (draft or pointer unreadable, fence stamp error), and a cancel during the wait. OVERLAP_LOSSES reads `turn` as 'lost to another part of the request' and re-runs the part alone up to twice. A serial part holds the config (holdsConfig), so the re-run takes the turn from its start and meets the same fault.
